Name: FlexWorld Series 2024 Recap: Insights and Predictions for the Future of Flex Spaces
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: FlexWorld Series is OfficeRnD’s annual virtual conference for coworking and flex space operators, where industry leaders share strategies on growth, operations, hospitality, and workspace technology.
Post body:
FlexWorld Series is OfficeRnD’s annual virtual conference for coworking and flex space operators, where industry leaders share strategies on growth, operations, hospitality, and workspace technology.

This is a recap of the FlexWorld Series 2024 conference, held virtually on Tuesday, May 21st. You can still watch every session on demand and follow the latest edition at the FlexWorld Series website.

Since its first edition, FlexWorld has become a leading event in the coworking industry, bringing together operators, industry professionals, and product teams to discuss trends, challenges, and opportunities in the sector.

The 2024 program drew participants from around the world across four panel sessions:

  • Growth vs Efficiency: Finding the Right Balance
  • Measure What Matters: Coworking KPIs, Benchmarks, and Industry Standards
  • Hospitality as a Competitive Edge
  • Navigating Tomorrow’s Technology Innovations (Product Roadmap)

Here’s what each session covered.

Growth vs Efficiency: Finding the Right Balance

One of the standout sessions was the panel discussion, “Growth vs Efficiency: Finding the Right Balance.” It brought together operators to work through the balance between expanding a flex space business and keeping operations efficient.

Moderated by Samantha Kenney, CMO at OfficeRnD, the panel shared strategies and real-world examples covering the tradeoffs between growth and efficiency.

The panelists were:

  • Jonny Rosenblatt; Co-Founder, SpaceMade
  • Jamie Russo; CEO, Everything Coworking
  • Triona O’Neill; Director of Operations, Serendipity Labs
  • Radoslav Enchev; Senior Product Manager, OfficeRnD
  • Samantha Kenney; CMO, OfficeRnD

Key discussion points

  • Defining growth and efficiency
  • What metrics do you look at for optimization?

Beyond the obvious metrics like office occupancy, hot-desk sales, and membership sales, the panel pointed to sales activity, contracted revenue, and website sessions per site as useful data points.

Revenue per square foot came up as a metric many flex space operators dislike. Member satisfaction and member retention are commonly used to project ARR and gauge revenue stability.

  • What tradeoffs have you made for optimization? Does being efficient mean sacrificing growth?

Efficiency comes before growth. Build scalable operations and processes that serve your team and members. Automate member onboarding and deliver turn-key setups so members can start working within minutes.

Learn from each space and apply what you find. Every space gets better than the last because you keep iterating.

Read this blog post for a deeper look at the session and the tactics the panelists use to grow their spaces.

You can also watch the video recording of the session below:

Measure What Matters: Coworking KPIs, Benchmarks, and Industry Standards

This panel looked at the metrics that drive success in coworking, and where industry standards fall short.

Attendees learned what other operators use as benchmarks and how they compare their spaces against top-performing companies outside coworking to find room to grow.

Moderated by OfficeRnD’s Mihail Kyosev, the panel discussed the “Rule of 40” and measuring your organization against “Blue Whale” companies outside the coworking industry.

The speakers were:

  • Alexandra Livesey; COO, Clockwise Offices
  • Anna Levine; Chief Commercial Officer, Industrious
  • Miro Miroslavov; CEO, OfficeRnD
  • Mihail Kyosev; Senior Manager Product & Data, OfficeRnD Flex

Key discussion points

  • How often are you using data to make decisions?

The panel agreed on looking at data that predicts where the whole industry is heading, not just a snapshot of right now.

  • What are your top 3 KPIs daily? Monthly? Yearly?

Cost of sales is a key data point: where new deals come from and how much they cost the business. The Rule of 40 helps measure growth and profitability together.

Retention rates deserve frequent attention. Winning a new customer is expensive, so keeping the ones you have is the cheaper way to grow.

Checking NPS daily gives you the chance to act fast. If someone raises a concern, you can spot the problem and address it right away.

  • How do you evaluate whether your performance metrics meet expectations? Do you benchmark against industry standards, historical data, or specific targets?

You need a north star. Large, successful US companies outside coworking were studied and shared four traits: strong parent-level EBITDA margins, steady revenue growth, high net revenue retention, and low fixed cost as a percent of revenue.

The takeaway: coworking benchmarking and data-tracking standards are still low and rarely standardized.

Read this article for the full set of insights from the session. You can also watch the video recording below:

Hospitality as a Competitive Edge

The panel for this session included:

  • Kenny Kane; CEO, Firmspace
  • Ed Hobbs; National General Manager, X+Why
  • Ivan Guberkov; VP Product, OfficeRnD

They discussed hospitality in coworking and how it sets spaces apart in a competitive market.

Good service and a welcoming environment attract and keep members, and they raise overall satisfaction and loyalty.

Speakers shared practical tips for building hospitality into daily operations, from personal member interactions to a community-centric atmosphere.

A culture of hospitality drives member engagement and supports growth. Attendees left with clear steps for using hospitality to build a coworking experience members want to stay in.

Key discussion points

  • Expectations vary across coworking spaces. How do you define “hospitality” in your operations, and how has it kept you competitive?

Hospitality starts with the welcome: “hi, how are you, how can we help?” Focus on consistent touch points and stay hungry to find solutions. Make sure everyone has the tools and resources they need to come to work and be successful.

  • Inspired by Will Guidara’s concept of “unreasonable hospitality,” can you share an example where going beyond expectations changed your space’s reputation or client loyalty?

A playbook helps, but what makes a space engaging is people’s personalities coming through, so let your team be authentic. Track metrics that aren’t only revenue-based but also measure the relationships you build with members.

Read this blog post for the practical tips and strategies Ed Hobbs and Kenny Kane shared.

You can also watch the video recording of the session below:

Navigating Tomorrow’s Technology Innovations

OfficeRnD’s Ivan Guberkov, VP of Product, ran this session solo, walking through where coworking technology is heading and what OfficeRnD Flex would ship next.

OfficeRnD Flex is a coworking management platform that automates operations, billing, bookings, and member experience for flex space operators.

The talk covered recent releases plus a preview of upcoming features for coworking operations and member experience, including tools that cut admin and payment work, improve benchmarking and data tracking, and support community engagement.

Since then, OfficeRnD Flex has grown into six connected hubs: Operations, Experience, Growth, Visitor, Data, and Integrations. Read the OfficeRnD Flex product year in review for the latest on what’s shipped, from dynamic pricing in Growth Hub to benchmarking in Data Hub.

You can also watch a video of the session below:

In conclusion

FlexWorld Series 2024 covered the ground that matters most to operators: measuring the right KPIs, using hospitality to compete, and reading where coworking technology is going.

Together, the sessions gave coworking operators concrete strategies they can put to work.

Thanks again to every speaker, attendee, and team member who made the event happen.

For updates on future editions, follow the conference site at https://flexworld.io/. You can also follow OfficeRnD on social media and read the blog to keep up with coworking insights.

Questions asked in the chat during the conference

What’s the most effective marketing channel for promoting private offices?

Google Ads drove the most success for the operators on the panel.

How do you build partnerships with other businesses to improve member benefits?

Kenny Kane, CEO at Firmspace, uses a platform called Paylode to build business connections that directly benefit members.

How can we get members to come to the office more often? We host monthly appreciation and in-house events, but it doesn’t help much.

Try incentives like discounted rates for frequent users and partnerships with local businesses for exclusive member discounts.

For events, keep testing new formats until one sticks, and survey members on what they actually want to attend.

Start with the space itself: appealing amenities and a good layout. Then experiment.

How do you monitor NPS without bombarding members?

Build real relationships and ask for open, honest feedback throughout the membership and at renewal.

We want to use the Brivo mobile app but have waited months for Apple to approve our developer account. Any tips?

This is case-specific, but Apple usually explains what the problem is and how to fix it. Reach out and ask for detail on exactly what’s required. A large developer community deals with the same requirements, so most issues have already been discussed and documented.

Name: Growth Vs Efficiency: Finding The Right Balance for Coworking Space Success
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: In the world of flexible workspaces, finding the right balance between growth and efficiency is essential for success.
Post body:
In the world of flexible workspaces, finding the right balance between growth and efficiency is essential for success.

How do you find that sweet spot?

Growth and efficiency are the two forces every coworking operator has to balance: growth adds members, locations, and revenue, while efficiency makes sure each of those additions actually pays off instead of straining the business.

This post covers insights from industry experts shared during a panel discussion at FlexWorld Series 2024, with practical guidance for flexible workspace operators.

The panel featured Jonny Rosenblatt, co-founder of Spacemade, Jamie Russo, host of the Everything Coworking Podcast, Triona O’Neill, Director of Operations at Serendipity Labs, Samantha Kenney, CMO at OfficeRnD, and Radoslav Enchev, senior product manager at OfficeRnD.

The experts shared their strategies and personal experiences in improving efficiency without sacrificing growth.

Let’s jump right in.

Understanding efficiency and growth

Efficiency

Efficiency in flexible workspaces breaks down into three main areas:

  1. Revenue efficiency: Maximizing income from available resources.
  2. Employment efficiency: Getting the most from staff productivity and satisfaction.
  3. Footprint optimization: Using space effectively to maximize occupancy and user experience.

Revenue efficiency means generating maximum income from each square foot and each member.

You get there through strategic pricing, upselling services, and adjusting membership plans to suit different needs.

Employment efficiency focuses on ensuring that staff are not only productive but also satisfied, as happy employees are more likely to contribute positively to the business.

Footprint optimization is about making the most of available space, balancing private offices, dedicated desks, and communal areas to create an appealing and functional environment.

Growth

Growth involves expanding the number of spaces, increasing membership, and adding to your service offerings. Growth has to be managed carefully so it doesn’t compromise efficiency.

Expansion can mean opening new locations, increasing the capacity of existing ones, or diversifying services to meet changing market demands.

Growth brings more revenue and market presence, but it also introduces challenges: maintaining service quality, managing larger teams, and making sure operational efficiency scales with the business.

Which metrics should you track?

To grow and stay efficient, operators should focus on several key metrics:

  • Occupancy rates: Track the percentage of space used at any given time. High occupancy shows effective use of space, but it needs balancing to avoid overcrowding.
  • Revenue per member: Measure the average income generated per member. This shows each member’s financial contribution and informs pricing decisions.
  • Net member gain: Calculate the difference between new memberships and cancellations. Positive net gain shows growth; negative trends need addressing to retain members.
  • Sales activity: Monitor viewings, inquiries, and contracts at various stages. An active sales funnel signals strong demand and effective marketing.
  • Website traffic and conversions: Measure digital engagement and conversion rates from tours to memberships. This tells you how well your online marketing is working.
  • Member retention and satisfaction: Use metrics like Net Promoter Score (NPS) to gauge member happiness and loyalty. High retention and satisfaction are critical for long-term stability.

  • Measure What Matters in Coworking: KPIs, Benchmarks and Industry Standards
  • Mastering Hospitality: How Exceptional Service Elevates Your Flex Space in a Competitive Market
  • FlexWorld Series 2024 Recap: Insights and Predictions for the Future of Flex Spaces

How do you balance efficiency and growth?

So, how do you actually balance efficiency and growth?

Jonny Rosenblatt made the case for transparency with landlord partners and detailed tracking of key metrics.

Spacemade shares real-time data with partners to keep everyone aligned and performance on track. That transparency covers sales activity, contracted revenue, and average desk rates, giving a clear picture of performance and where to improve.

Jamie Russo pointed to the tension between hospitality and profitability. She argued that revenue per square foot is a critical metric, even though it can conflict with creating a good member experience.

Disciplined metric tracking keeps you efficient. She also stressed that maximizing revenue per square foot shouldn’t come at the expense of member experience, since satisfied members stay longer and refer others.

For Triona O’Neill, member retention and satisfaction come first, measured with NPS. Serendipity Labs keeps retention high and stability long-term by prioritizing member experience and using technology to simplify processes.

A welcoming, supportive community matters here. Happy members stay loyal and contribute to a positive atmosphere.

Effective marketing strategies

Community building and referrals

Triona stressed the value of community building through local partnerships and events. Serendipity Labs hosts events to build connections. This strengthens their brand and brings in new members through word-of-mouth.

Word of mouth is the top way new customers find a coworking space, according to OfficeRnD’s industry trends report. Learn more here. Events build a strong community and double as networking opportunities for members, adding value to their membership.

Always-on digital marketing

Jonny discussed Spacemade’s always-on digital marketing approach, including Google Ads, Instagram Ads, and LinkedIn campaigns. A continuous digital presence keeps visibility up and drives inquiries.

He shared a billboard campaign targeting local commuters that noticeably lifted inquiries and conversions. The key is consistent, engaging content that resonates with the target audience and keeps a steady flow of potential members coming in.

Experimentation and tracking

Jamie Russo emphasized testing different marketing strategies and tracking results. Different markets need different approaches, so you have to test and measure what works.

She also noted that a strong online presence is critical in competitive markets. That means paid advertising, content marketing, social media engagement, and search engine optimization (SEO).

Advice for scaling operations

Use technology

Triona O’Neill advised using technology to simplify processes and improve member experience. It plays a big role in Serendipity Labs’ success.

Efficient systems let you scale without dropping service quality.

Technology automates routine tasks, gives you insights through data, and improves communication both inside the team and with members.

OfficeRnD Flex is coworking management software that automates billing, bookings, and member operations from one platform. Its AI Hub adds an automation layer inside Flex, starting with an AI Sales Agent that responds to inbound leads around the clock so a form submitted at 9 PM doesn’t sit until the next morning.

Keep the business model simple

A simple business model that meets customer needs while keeping processes scalable is essential.

Complexity slows growth, so keep things straightforward: clear service offerings, simple pricing, and flexible membership plans that are easy to manage and scale.

Hire startup-minded people

From experience, Jonny Rosenblatt recommended hiring people with a startup mentality: those willing to take on multiple roles and drive growth from the ground up.

That mindset builds a strong base for scaling. People with a startup mentality tend to be more adaptable, more resourceful, and more committed to the company’s success, which matters most during the growth phase.

Be calculated and intentional

Jamie Russo cautioned against reverse-engineering what works for others, since it might not be sustainable. Focus on calculated risks and have a clear plan for scaling.

She suggested getting advice from experienced operators and staying conservative with expenses until the business can support the added overhead.

Understand the specific needs and context of your business rather than following trends blindly.

In conclusion

Balancing growth and efficiency in flexible workspaces takes a clear strategy, good data, the right technology, and a strong team. Prioritize member experience and stay intentional with expansion, and you can grow sustainably without letting operations slip.

The insights from our panel give operators a practical guide for this work.

By tracking the right metrics, running marketing that actually converts, and making smart hires, operators can build efficient workspaces that keep up with what their members need.

Name: Mastering Hospitality: How Exceptional Service Elevates Your Flex Space in a Competitive Market
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: In coworking, hospitality is what sets a full house apart from a churning one. This post pulls together advice from two operators who ran the numbers and the front desk, shared during a panel at FlexWorld Series .
Post body:
In coworking, hospitality is what sets a full house apart from a churning one. This post pulls together advice from two operators who ran the numbers and the front desk, shared during a panel at FlexWorld Series.

Hospitality in a flex space is the day-to-day service that makes members feel welcomed, supported, and equipped to do their best work, from the first hello to every problem you solve after.

The panel featured Ed Hobbs, National General Manager, x+why and Kenny Kane, CEO, Firmspace. Both shared how they run efficient operations without cutting the service that keeps members renewing.

What does hospitality mean in a flex space?

For Ed Hobbs, hospitality is the combination of a warm welcome, consistent touchpoints, and a genuine hunger for solutions throughout a member’s journey.

For x+why, adaptability and responsiveness keep them competitive. They operate on managed service agreements with a range of landlords, from city councils to large banks, each with different needs.

That flexibility lets them tailor hospitality to each site and build a community where members collaborate and learn from one another.

Kenny Kane of Firmspace frames hospitality around outcomes: making sure members have the resources they need to be successful every day.

Firmspace builds around privacy, security, and productivity, and its service supports those three pillars.

Kane focuses on removing friction in both the physical and digital sides of the workspace, so members get a clean experience end to end.

Interested in learning more about the latest coworking and flex space trends shaping the industry? This free industry report contains invaluable insights, tips, and data. 

How do you measure the impact of hospitality?

Ed Hobbs admits this is hard to measure. Net Promoter Score (NPS) helps, but he treats it as the opening of a deeper conversation, not a final verdict on how you’re doing.

Hobbs stresses the importance of creating a brand where world-class hospitality is the norm, lowering barriers to entry and encouraging collaboration.

Firmspace also uses NPS, but leans on strong member relationships to catch concerns before they turn into problems.

Kane sees the frontline of hospitality as daily engagement: clear communication and aligned expectations from the first day.

If you want harder numbers, tie hospitality to retention. Track renewal rates, churn reasons, and how many issues get resolved on the first ask. Small, remembered details compound: retention in coworking rarely comes down to one feature, and instead builds through repeated moments where members feel recognized, as Hector Kolonas of Syncaroo put it. Capture a few preferences at onboarding, what people drink or snack on, and use them later.

How do you put hospitality into practice?

Training and consistency

Hobbs and Kane agree that training and consistency carry the load. Hobbs lets team members’ personalities come through, which keeps the service authentic rather than scripted.

At Firmspace, Kane uses an app called Trainual to document core hospitality principles and reinforce them during training and team meetings.

  • FlexWorld Series Recap: Insights and Predictions for the Future of Flex Spaces
  • Growth Vs Efficiency: Finding The Right Balance for Coworking Space Success
  • Measure What Matters in Coworking: KPIs, Benchmarks and Industry Standards

Relentless troubleshooting

Kane coined “relentless troubleshooting” for Firmspace’s approach to member support. Staff move quickly on issues, technical or otherwise, so members can stay focused on their work.

It also helps to use the network effect to build community, so members bring value to each other, not just to you.

Amenities and strategies that support hospitality

x+why’s multifunctional spaces

Hobbs said x+why keeps its spaces as versatile as possible. That includes designing areas that reconfigure easily for different events and uses, so every square foot earns its keep.

They also track member preferences and personalize service around them.

Firmspace’s hybrid strategy

Firmspace runs a hybrid work strategy to match how businesses use offices now.

Multiple people from the same company can use the office on different days, which preserves the quality of the experience while supporting flexible schedules.

Small gestures with big impact

Hobbs told a story about a senior community manager who noticed a member acting differently and stopped to offer support.

That small kindness built a real personal connection and showed how genuine care strengthens member relationships.

Kane takes pride in still having Firmspace’s very first member. By delivering on their promises and staying close to members, the team earns loyalty and mutual respect.

How do you balance efficiency and hospitality?

In a flex space, hospitality and operational efficiency work together.

Hobbs pushes his team to cut waste and get creative with resources. x+why sources locally and finds second uses for materials.

This approach saves costs and fits their commitment to sustainability and community.

Kane set up an “honest market” to replace standard office snacks with premium options chosen from member feedback. It cuts waste and adds convenience and value for members.

The efficiency piece is also where software earns its place. When billing, bookings, and member requests run on their own, your team spends its hours in the space with members instead of in spreadsheets. OfficeRnD Flex automates the member lifecycle, billing, and bookings so your community team can focus on service. Its AI Hub goes a step further: an AI sales agent that qualifies leads and handles bookings around the clock, so no prospect waits while your team focuses on hospitality.

The takeaway

Hospitality as a competitive edge takes a plan that pairs efficient operations with real care for members.

Prioritize member experience, build relationships that last, and give your team the tools and freedom to solve problems fast. That’s how operators keep spaces full in a crowded market. The advice from Ed Hobbs and Kenny Kane gives you a workable model for getting there.

Name: Creating An Optimal Coworking Space Floor Plan [Full Guide]
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: With the coworking market estimated to reach 35.63 billion by 2032, there has never been a better time to open a coworking space.
Post body:
With the coworking market estimated to reach 35.63 billion by 2032, there has never been a better time to open a coworking space.

But before you create your coworking space floor plan, it’s crucial you understand the key elements of successful design.

This article will delve into everything to consider when designing the best possible coworking space floor plan.

Quick Summary

  • A coworking space floor plan is crucial to ensuring optimal member productivity, happiness, and well-being.
  • Consider the following when deciding on your coworking space floor plan: privacy, amenities, furniture, visuals, and members’ ability to collaborate.
  • Your coworking space floor plan should include an open desk area, private offices, lounge areas, meeting spaces, and more, depending on your target members.

Why Is a Coworking Space Floor Plan Important?

Choosing an optimal floor plan is vital for the productivity of your members — and it impacts the success of your entire business model. A poorly designed floor plan can hinder collaboration, lead to poor concentration and impact worker health. That will affect your NPS (net promoter score) and cost you money.

Shared spaces are important, as they encourage social interactions and collaboration. Community spaces are particularly vital since 20% of remote workers report loneliness as a major challenge in their lives.

Furthermore, collaborative layouts have proven financial benefits — 50% of individuals starting a coworking space arrangement see increases in their income.

Things to Consider When Designing a Coworking Space

Creating a coworking space that meets the needs of diverse members requires a balanced approach to design. Each element plays a crucial role in how effectively the space serves its members, from encouraging focus to maximizing comfort.

Here are the key factors to consider when planning your coworking space layout:

Collaboration and Community

One study concluded that having environments with the potential to facilitate collaborations is crucial to the success of a coworking space. To create collaborative setups that inspire creativity, innovation, and professional growth, try incorporating the following:

  • Large tables: These are essential for group projects and brainstorming sessions, allowing for the easy sharing of ideas and resources.
  • Shared meeting spaces: Well-equipped meeting rooms that can be booked as needed encourage formal and informal team collaboration sessions.
  • Open seating areas: Designed to facilitate spontaneous conversations and interactions, these areas can help form and strengthen professional networks.
  • Event spaces: A versatile event space is invaluable for hosting workshops, talks, and social events, all of which enrich the community experience.
  • Green spaces – sustainable coworking spaces are on the rise and attract many people interested in green initiatives.

Privacy

Despite the benefits of open spaces, privacy remains important for many professionals. Fifty-eight percent of office workers claim that having access to private work areas allows them to produce their best work.

To accommodate the need for privacy, include the following in your coworking space floor plan:

  • Small offices: These are ideal for small companies or individuals that require concentration or confidentiality.
  • Conference rooms: These spaces are crucial for teams to conduct private discussions without external disruptions.
  • Phone booths: These small, enclosed spaces are perfect for private calls and video meetings.

Do you want to succeed in a crowded market in 2024 and beyond? Multiple successful spaces cite hospitality as a competitive edge. Want to know how to do it properly, like seasoned pros do? Download this free report. It has all the answers. 

Amenities

The right amenities can significantly enhance the attractiveness of a coworking space. These include the following:

  • High-speed internet: This is a non-negotiable feature in today’s global, digital working era.
  • 24-hour access: This allows members to work according to their own schedules.
  • Cafe and bar areas: Members can unwind and socialize in these spaces.
  • Wellness facilities: Gyms, yoga classes, and meditation rooms can improve member well-being.
  • Functional amenities: Meeting rooms, printers, scanners, and personal lockers add everyday convenience for all members.
  • Childcare: Some coworking spaces, like Big and Tiny, offer childcare for working parents.

Sizing and Space Distribution

The size of your coworking space should reflect the needs of your membership base. Coworking spaces typically range from 50 to 200 people and hold a combination of office spaces for small businesses and hot desks for individuals and freelancers. Depending on your goals, you may prefer to cater to one or the other or a mix of both.

The global average size of a coworking space is around 7,244 square feet, and it’s typical to see a space split of 70/30 or 50/50 between workspace and communal areas. This balance helps to meet your members’ collaborative and private needs.

Furniture

Your choice of furniture can greatly influence the functionality and atmosphere of your coworking space. In addition to sufficient working desks and chairs, consider incorporating:

  • Couches and casual seating: These are great for relaxation and less formal work.
  • Ergonomic office furniture: Standing desks and adjustable chairs can promote health and comfort.
  • Large tables and desks: These facilitate collaboration and individual work, with ample space for equipment.

Visuals

The aesthetic of your coworking space can hugely impact employee satisfaction, well-being, and productivity. Visual elements to consider include:

  • Interior design: Choose a theme that reflects your brand’s identity and appeals to your target audience.
  • Lighting: Natural light sources are preferable, but they can be supplemented by artificial lighting that enhances focus and energy.

Check out Work Better to see how they do that really well.

Noise Management

Managing noise levels is crucial in a shared workspace. Strategies to consider include the following:

  • Layout design: Strategically place noisy areas away from quiet zones.
  • Soundproofing: Implement sound-absorbing materials in key areas, like phone booths or conference rooms.

6 Essentials Every Coworking Space Floor Plan Must Have

When designing a coworking space, ensuring every area contributes to the key goals of productivity, collaboration, and networking is essential.

Here are six essentials every coworking space floor plan should include to meet the diverse needs of its members:

Open Desk Space

Open desk space is at the heart of any coworking space. This layout caters primarily to freelancers, who constituted 37% of coworking space members in 2023.

Open desks encourage a flexible work style and enhance the interactions among members. You can even use software to facilitate coworking booking.

Private Offices

Small, private offices are essential for groups or individuals who require more privacy and a controlled environment to focus on their work. These spaces are ideal for small teams and professionals who frequently handle confidential information.

Meeting Rooms

Including versatile meeting spaces equipped with smart screens and other equipment helps facilitate team discussions and external client meetings. Smaller phone booths are also helpful for private calls and video conferences. For example, Codebase, a premium coworking space in Virginia, US, has very appealing meeting booths.

Lounge Areas

Lounge areas are informal spaces where members can relax, network, and socialize. They help build a sense of community within the coworking environment, making them essential for member satisfaction and retention.

Event Spaces

Incorporating a dedicated area for events, such as a bar or multipurpose room, allows for professional workshops, social gatherings, and networking events. This adds value to the membership and actively supports the community-building aspect of coworking spaces.

Amenities

Offering a range of amenities, such as a well-equipped kitchen, high-quality coffee and snacks, and wellness facilities, enhances the overall coworking experience and convenience for members. In one survey, members voted wellness amenities as the most desired amenity.

A Step-by-Step Guide to Creating Your Own Coworking Space Floor Plan

Meet the needs of your coworking space members and maximize your space for return on investment with the following steps:

Evaluate the Space

Start by assessing the total square footage available to you. Consider the shape and limitations of the space, such as columns, windows, and exits.

Determine Your Target Audience

Know who your space will serve. Are your primary clients freelancers who might prefer open and flexible environments, or are they start-ups and companies that might need private offices and dedicated desks?

Define Distinct Areas

Segment the space into clearly defined areas based on your target users’ needs. Essential zones include an open desk space for hot desking, offices for start-ups and businesses, and meeting rooms for privacy.

Add common spaces like lounges and kitchens to encourage networking and relaxation.

Consider the Space’s Services and Amenities

Decide on the amenities and services that will enhance the coworking experience. Modern coworking spaces offer many innovative options, from high-speed internet and printing facilities to virtual mailboxes and fitness centers.

Avoid Possible Pitfalls

Plan the layout to minimize noise in focus areas by strategically placing noisy activities (like phone calls and meetings) away from quiet zones. Use design elements, such as soundproofing panels and the strategic placement of furniture, to help reduce distractions.

Examples of Coworking Space Floor Plans

To guarantee yourself success, it’s crucial to optimize your floor plan to be the ideal mix of functional and economically viable. Here’s how to structure different floor plans based on space sizes and member capacities:

Small Coworking Space Floor Plan

For spaces designed to accommodate between 50 and 100 members, a compact yet efficient design works best. Include a generous number of hot desks for freelancers and hybrid and remote workers who don’t require a traditional office space.

Also, add a few private meeting rooms and comfortable common areas for relaxation and informal interactions.

Medium Coworking Space Floor Plan

In medium-sized spaces that cater to 100 to 150 members, there is room for a bit more specialization in the use of space.

Along with hot desks, incorporate a few small private offices that can be rented out to small start-ups or remote teams. Plenty of meeting rooms and common areas for larger gatherings will accommodate the wide range of users in these spaces.

Large Coworking Space Floor Plan

Bigger spaces typically serve between 150 and 200 members, although some larger-scale operations hold up to 8,000 seats.

Post body:
In the corporate world, meetings are the lifeblood of collaboration, innovation, and decision-making. Whether it’s a brainstorming session, a crucial client presentation, or a routine team check-in, the environment you create can significantly impact the outcome.

One often overlooked yet vital component of this environment is catering. The right catering can transform a mundane meeting into a memorable experience, fostering engagement and boosting morale.

However, planning, organizing, and ordering the perfect meeting room catering is no small feat. Corporate managers, business executives, and facility managers face a myriad of challenges in this endeavor.

The logistics can be daunting, from accommodating diverse dietary preferences and ensuring timely delivery to maintaining budget constraints and aligning with the company’s sustainability goals.

Moreover, in today’s hybrid work environment, where teams are often split between in-office and remote locations, the complexity of coordinating catering services increases manifold.

Understanding these challenges and navigating them effectively is crucial for delivering an exceptional meeting experience that leaves a lasting impression. In this blog post, we will delve into the essentials of planning, organizing, and ordering the perfect meeting room catering, providing you with practical tips and insights to elevate your next corporate gathering.

Quick Summary

  • Planning weeks in advance is crucial for organizing meeting room catering
  • Using the right technology to book the meeting space and the catering will save you time and effort
  • Understanding the food preferences of meeting attendees is paramount to avoid cringe-worthy moments
  • Some original catering ideas include build-your-own salad bar, healthy snack stations, and gourmet coffee and tea bar

Understanding Your Audience

In the bustling realm of office dynamics, the importance of understanding your audience cannot be overstated, especially when it comes to catering. It’s a good sign of proper meeting room etiquette. It’s not only a question of “who will be attending your gathering”, but also “what are their expectations?”

The first step in planning a meeting with catering is understanding your audience’s culinary preferences.

Are they health-conscious individuals who prefer light and nutritious options? Are they adventurous foodies who enjoy bold flavors and exotic cuisines? Do they have allergies or dietary restrictions?

Will they feel comfortable eating specific foods in front of other attendees? Gathering insights into your audience’s tastes and preferences is a must and doesn’t have to be as daunting as it sounds.

Psst...! You can now book meeting rooms in Microsoft Teams!

Gathering Insights

FARE, also known as Food Allergy Research & Education, have found that 1 in 10 adult Americans have food-related allergies and more than 170 different foods have been known to cause allergic reactions.

I don’t know about you, but I don’t think I can even name 170 different foods – how do we know what people can and cannot have? This is why collecting information from your attendees prior to your meeting is crucial.

Aside from allergies, organizations today are putting more of a focus on diversity and inclusion and dietary preferences are top of mind when it comes to meeting room catering. From vegan, keto, and gluten-free to Halal and Kosher, understanding your audience means anticipating and accommodating these dietary needs.

We’ve found the following methods to be the most helpful when collecting dietary data for meetings and events:

  1. Pre-Event Surveys – Send out a comprehensive survey to attendees well in advance of the event. Include questions about dietary preferences, allergies, intolerances, and any specific requirements they may have.
  2. Event Registration Forms – For larger events, incorporating dietary preference questions into the event registration process can be helpful. When attendees sign up for the event, the registration form will prompt them to provide information about their dietary restrictions and preferences.
  3. Direct Communication – When sending a calendar invite for an in-person meeting, encourage attendees to reach out directly if they have specific dietary restrictions or requirements. Provide contact information for attendees to contact event organizers or catering staff to discuss their needs confidentially.

Planning the Perfect Menu

Planning the perfect menu is an art form that requires careful consideration of your audience’s preferences, dietary restrictions, and the overall tone of the event. Crafting an exceptional culinary experience goes beyond simply serving food; it involves curating a menu that delights the senses and enhances the meeting room atmosphere.

Let’s dive into how to plan the perfect menu.

Diversifying Menu Options to Satisfy Dietary Needs

Diversity in menu options is key to accommodating the varied tastes and dietary needs of meeting attendees.

Offering a wide range of menu choices, including vegetarian or vegan, gluten-free, and so many others, ensures that all attendees can enjoy delicious and satisfying meals that align with their individual preferences and restrictions.

Nutritional Food vs. Comfort Food: Finding the Right Balance

Finding the perfect balance between healthy options and comfort foods is essential for catering to the diverse preferences of meeting attendees.

You’ll want to consider a thoughtful selection of nutritious offerings such as fresh salads, grilled vegetables, lean protein, and fresh fruit, alongside comforting classics like sandwiches, pasta salads, and artisanal pizzas.

By striking this balance, we ensure that attendees can indulge in satisfying meals while also making healthy choices that support their well-being.

The Art of Timing and Presenting Meals During Meetings

The presentation and timing of meal services play a crucial role in enhancing the overall meeting experience.

It is important to pay close attention to every detail, from the visual appeal of the dishes to the timing of the meal service, ensuring a seamless and enjoyable dining experience for all attendees.

Whether it’s a plated meal service for more formal meetings or a buffet-style spread for casual gatherings, it is also important to time the service correctly so that it does not interfere with the meeting at hand.

Meeting Room Catering Ideas

If you’re looking for some inspiration to elevate your meeting room catering, here are some creative ideas to consider:

  • Build-Your-Own Salad Bar: Set up a DIY salad bar with an array of fresh greens, colorful vegetables, protein options, and flavorful dressings, allowing attendees to customize their salads to their liking. You can also take this one step further and have a different themed DIY Bar, a Taco Bar or a Mac and Cheese bar, for example. All you need to do is supply the base, or the main ingredients, and include toppings, sauces, dressings, etc. for each attendee to make their meal their own way.
  • Healthy Snack Stations: Keep attendees energized and focused with a selection of nutritious snacks such as fresh fruit skewers, yogurt parfaits, granola bars, and vegetable platters. These items are great to keep on a side table or in the back of the room for attendees to grab when they need to stand and stretch their legs after a long day of meetings.
  • Gourmet Coffee and Tea Bar: Elevate coffee breaks with a gourmet coffee and tea bar featuring specialty coffee blends, artisanal teas, and decadent accompaniments such as gourmet pastries, cookies, and chocolate truffles.

By incorporating some of these ideas into your meeting room gatherings, you can delight attendees with memorable culinary experiences that have a lasting impression.

Organizing Meeting Logistics

Organizing a meeting involves meticulous planning, especially when catering is involved. From estimating quantities to optimizing the meeting room (or huddle room) setup for efficient food service, every detail contributes to a smooth and successful event.

Estimating Food Quantities with Accuracy

Accurately estimating quantities is essential to ensure that attendees are well-fed without excessive waste. Consider the following factors when estimating how much food to order for your next work meeting:

  1. Number of Attendees: Start by determining the number of attendees expected at the meeting. Take RSVPs into account, but also factor in potential last-minute additions or cancellations.
  2. Meeting Duration: Consider the duration of the meeting when planning catering. Longer meetings may require additional refreshments or meal/snack breaks to keep attendees energized and focused.
  3. Menu Selection: Choose menu items that are appropriate for the meeting duration and time of day. For shorter meetings, light snacks and beverages may suffice, while longer meetings may necessitate more substantial meal options. Additionally, you can often get away with a smaller selection with breakfast and lunch services, whereas meetings that go until or through dinner time often require more of a standard meal.
  4. Dietary Preferences: Take into account any dietary preferences or restrictions indicated by attendees when estimating quantities. Ensure that there are sufficient options available for all meeting participants.

Setting Up the Meeting Room for Efficient Food Service

Efficient food service relies on thoughtful planning and consideration of the meeting room layout. Factors like where the food is located, the flow of the room and accessibility, and even signage, play pivotal roles in the fluidity of your event.

When designing the layout of the meeting room space, designate a specific area of the meeting room for food and beverage service. After hours of sitting through presentations or brainstorming new ideas, all your attendees will be thinking, “what is the fastest route to the food table?”

With a specific area for the food to be set up, you’ll alleviate any congestion as folks start moving about and getting their food. Buffet tables or stations in a centralized location are the best for quick and easy access. Keep in mind the layout of the room and try not to align your food stations with obstacles or barriers that may impede the flow of traffic or create bottlenecks.

When planning your meeting space, you should also ensure that food and beverage stations are easily accessible to all attendees, including those with mobility challenges or disabilities.

Consider the placement of tables, chairs, and serving counters and determine the best way to accommodate everyone comfortably.

Signage, though depending on the style can sometimes feel a bit tacky, can often be extremely helpful. Clear signage that guides attendees to food and beverage stations and indicates menu options, dietary information, and allergen warnings can help reduce confusion during meal service.

You can also include signage for dirty dishes or trash and recycling to ensure guests know where to put their empty plates once they’ve finished.

Sustainable Catering Options

In the modern era, sustainability has become a pressing concern across all areas of business operations, and that doesn’t leave out meetings and events.

As businesses strive to reduce their environmental footprint, the catering industry has responded by offering eco-friendly options that prioritize sustainability without compromising the overall catering experience.

The Importance of Making Eco-Friendly Catering Choices

The food industry is a significant contributor to environmental degradation, with issues such as food waste, carbon emissions, and plastic pollution posing serious threats to the environment.

According to the United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), over one-third of the food produced in the United States is never eaten. Their research has shown that food waste is the “single most common material landfilled and incinerated in the U.S.”

How To Choose Sustainable Catering Options

  1. Source Locally and Seasonally: Choose catering providers that prioritize locally sourced and seasonal ingredients. Locally sourced foods require less transportation, reducing carbon emissions, and supporting local farms and producers. Seasonal ingredients are fresher, tastier, and more environmentally friendly than their out-of-season counterparts.
  2. Opt for Plant-Based Options: Plant-based foods have a lower environmental footprint compared to animal products and can help reduce greenhouse gas emissions, water, usage, and land degradation associated with animal agriculture.
  3. Reduce Single-Use Plastics: Choose catering providers that offer alternatives to single-use plastics such as compostable or reusable servingware, utensils, and packaging. Avoid individually packaged items and opt for bulk servings to minimize packaging waste.
  4. Minimize Food Waste: Work with catering providers to minimize food waste by accurately estimating the number of attendees and portion sizes. Consider donating surplus food to local charities or food banks rather than throwing it away. Encourage attendees to take leftovers home or provide composting bins for food scraps.
  5. Offer Water Stations: Instead of serving bottled water, provide water stations with reusable glassware or compostable cups. Encourage attendees to bring their reusable water bottles to refill throughout the event as well.
  6. Do you Research: Are you familiar with local establishments that provide sustainable catering options? Is there a local cafe where you can purchase soups, salads, and sandwiches, as well as fresh juices in glass jars? Maybe there is a business nearby that provides compostable packaging as well as servingware. Making informed decisions and using these options whenever possible is key to staying on track.

Out-of-the-Box Catering: Interactive Food Experiences

Let’s face it, engaging attendees and fostering connections are essential for a successful meeting. But who wants to sit through hours of boardroom conversations with no immediate payoff?

  • Sushi Rolling Station: Set up a sushi rolling station where attendees can learn to roll their own sushi rolls under the guidance of a sushi chef. Provide a variety of sushi-grade fish, vegetables, rice, and seaweed sheets, along with condiments like soy sauce, wasabi, and pickled ginger.
  • DIY Pizza Making: If your office has a stove in the kitchen/breakroom area, this next one will be a major hit! Transform your meeting room into a pizzeria with a DIY pizza-making station. Provide pre-made dough, a variety of sauces, cheeses, and toppings allowing attendees to customize their pizzas. You could also have everyone bring one topping to share to initiate conversation and collaboration.
  • Cooking Demonstrations: Host a cooking demonstration led by a professional chef who will showcase culinary techniques and recipes. You can choose from themes like healthy cooking, international cuisine, or seasonal specialties. The chef will most likely bring a tabletop griddle of sorts and attendees can observe the cooking process, ask questions, and sample the finished products.
  • Artisanal Ice Cream Sundae Bar: Indulge attendees’ sweet cravings with an artisanal dessert bar. Offer bases like brownies, cookies, donuts, or bananas for attendees to use as their base, and provide a variety of premium ice cream flavors. Make sure you don’t forget the toppings and sauces or have the attendees volunteer to bring in their favorites. Whether you’re a facility manager, team leader, or IT professional, it’s your job to make sure your conference rooms are equipped with solid tech. This guide walks you through the specific tech features we recommend for your conference room, plus how to choose and set up the right technology.

Quick Summary:

  • Must-have conference room technology includes wireless connectivity, room lighting systems, audio and video conferencing equipment, and meeting room booking software.
  • Following a few best practices helps you get a solid return on your tech investment.

Conference room technology is the set of audio, video, display, and booking tools that let people in a meeting room and people joining remotely see, hear, and work together clearly.

Why invest in conference room technology?

Whether your team works mostly hybrid or fully on-site, you need the right conference room technology for a productive meeting. Remote employees want to collaborate in real time and feel as if they’re in the same room.

As a manager, your job is to give team members what they need to do their best work. That means keeping up with conference room technology trends and equipment that supports productivity and collaboration.

Budgets aren’t unlimited, though. You may need to pick a single meeting room to have everything you want.

Other meeting rooms might have smaller sets of tech features. Some may have only the bare essentials.

Your goal as a facility manager is to invest in tech that keeps people coming back and avoids the cost of constant maintenance or turnover. Tools that serve diverse audiences keep your hybrid workplaces running.

Here’s a quick guide on how to set up a meeting room for success.

Now to the conference room specifics.

Are you using the right conference room booking software?

The best conference room technology for the workplace

There are many ways to improve your conference room and give attendees the experience they expect, and ultimately build high-tech conference rooms. Here are the main ones:

Room lighting systems

It makes little sense to invest in expensive cameras and displays if the room’s lighting is poor or even average. Remote conferencing and filming in-person presentations both require proper lighting.

Well-lit rooms also keep people focused, attentive, and productive. Pick the right system, such as one with motion sensors, and you can cut your facility’s energy use.

Here’s a good list of the best office lighting options.

And here are three brands known for conference room lighting systems:

  1. Philips Hue White and Color Ambiance: A smart lighting system that offers a wide range of colors and adjustable white light for any meeting. It can be controlled via a mobile app, voice commands, or an existing conference room control system, with customizable scenes for different meeting types, from presentations to brainstorming sessions.
  2. Lutron Vive: A wireless lighting control system that’s quick to install. It controls lights through wireless remotes, sensors, or mobile devices, and can integrate with other building systems. Vive lets users adjust lighting levels to match the task at hand, which saves energy and improves comfort.
  3. Crestron Zūm: A lighting control system built to scale from a single huddle space to a multi-room deployment. Zūm uses wireless dimmers, occupancy sensors, and daylight sensors to adjust lighting automatically, keeping the right amount of light for any activity while cutting energy use.

Wireless connectivity

Wireless connections remove the need for cumbersome cables. They make meeting setups simpler and keep the room more organized.

Many technologies depend on strong wireless connectivity, including:

  • Wireless presentation systems
  • Remote collaboration tools
  • Real-time content sharing

If you’re managing a facility, make sure your conference rooms can handle high-bandwidth demands, because multiple hybrid teams will likely need them at the same time.

Presentation and collaboration tools

Hybrid work is part of the equation now. It improves work-life balance, increases productivity, and supports healthier routines.

To keep virtual meetings and brainstorming sessions engaging, you need tools with clear visuals that let everyone take part. The software you choose should support high-definition video. Screen sharing and remote control access let presenters deliver more dynamic presentations.

Here are the presentation and collaboration tools worth considering:

  • High-definition projectors
  • Motorized screens or large fixed screens
  • Smartboards that allow touch input (more on that below)
  • Cameras (e.g., PTZ cameras for auto-tracking)
  • Microphones (e.g., boundary or ceiling microphones)
  • Speaker systems (high-quality audio output)
  • Integrated room systems (e.g., Cisco Webex Room Kits, Zoom Rooms, Microsoft Teams Rooms)

Working under a hybrid model? Here’s an in-depth article on the best hybrid meeting equipment.

Digital whiteboards and interactive displays

For effective collaboration between team members, no matter where they’re located, digital whiteboards help you deliver presentations. Users can also share documents and photos and interact across devices with these tools.

Interactive displays let people work directly with content, add notes, or make changes in real time. Touch screens, stylus pens, and the right software help teams brainstorm and visualize together.

Here are three whiteboard and interactive display options to consider:

  1. Microsoft Surface Hub: A touch-enabled display for team meetings and brainstorming. It integrates with Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams, and pairs with Microsoft Whiteboard for real-time co-editing across devices.
  2. SMART Boards: Interactive whiteboards with touch and multi-touch input for interactive presentations. They ship with SMART software used widely in corporate and educational settings for collaboration.
  3. Software whiteboards: Google discontinued Jamboard on December 31, 2024, and pointed users toward third-party whiteboard apps that integrate with Google Workspace. Miro, FigJam, and Microsoft Whiteboard are the common replacements, each offering an infinite canvas, templates, and real-time collaboration for remote and in-room participants.

Audio conferencing equipment

Sound needs careful attention when you set up or refurbish a modern conference room. Clear audio keeps people focused and involved.

Several systems use noise and echo cancellation. Some feature AI-powered mixers and denoisers so audio stays clear as conditions change.

These tools give the conference room a professional feel.

Here are three brands known for audio conferencing equipment:

  1. Poly (formerly Polycom): Poly offers audio conferencing solutions, including conference phones like the Poly Trio series, with noise cancellation and full-duplex audio for clear communication.
  2. Yamaha: Yamaha’s ADECIA conferencing solution combines ceiling, tabletop, or wireless microphones with a conference processor, network switch, and speakers. It uses adaptive echo cancellation, Human Voice Activity Detection, and auto-tuning so a room can be configured in a few steps.
  3. Jabra: Jabra makes audio conferencing devices, including the Jabra Speak series of portable speakerphones with clear sound, simple controls, and connectivity to common conferencing platforms.

Speakers and microphones

Now to get specific about the audio, starting with microphones.

Remote participants need to hear and be heard by everyone else in the meeting. Quality microphones capture sound from across the room.

A large venue may benefit from one or more ceiling-mounted microphones or speakers. A smaller meeting room might do fine with conventional microphones and wall-mounted speakers.

Microphone systems with directional capabilities or automatic speaker detection can adapt to who’s speaking and where they are in the room.

Here are three brands known for conference room microphones:

  1. Shure: Shure offers conferencing microphones including the MXA920 and MXA910 ceiling array mics and the MXA310 table array mic, which capture clear audio with beamforming technology.
  2. Audio-Technica: Audio-Technica makes conferencing microphones such as the ATND971a cardioid condenser boundary microphone, known for clarity and easy integration into conferencing systems.
  3. Sennheiser: Sennheiser offers conference room microphones including the TeamConnect Ceiling 2 and the MEB 133-S table boundary microphone, with features like automatic beamforming and remote management.

Video conferencing equipment

Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, and Zoom on their own aren’t always enough. It gets awkward when some people are around a table in a meeting room while others join virtually.

You need video conferencing hardware to capture clear video. You also need to show remote participants and content on a big screen or video wall.

Put that together with a good sound kit and you get a meeting where communication stays clear and productive.

Here are three brands known for video conferencing equipment:

  1. Logitech makes the popular Rally series: video conferencing systems with modular audio, PTZ (pan-tilt-zoom) capabilities, and Ultra-HD video. The Rally Bar and Rally Bar Plus are popular for their video and audio performance. Logitech MeetUp is a compact, all-in-one camera for huddle rooms and smaller spaces, with a wide-angle lens, integrated speakers, and microphones.
  2. Cisco offers Webex Room Kits: video conferencing systems that work with the Cisco Webex platform. They include cameras, microphones, and speakers, with features like speaker tracking and AI-driven camera framing. Cisco also makes higher-end systems for larger boardrooms.
  3. Poly (formerly Polycom) offers the Studio X series: all-in-one video bars with high-quality video and audio. The Studio X30, X50, and X52 are known for simplicity, AI-driven camera framing, and support for common conferencing platforms. The Poly G7500 is a modular system that combines content sharing and video conferencing for medium to large rooms.

High-definition cameras

The camera is a key part of any video conferencing system.

There are many options, including:

  • 4K HD cameras
  • Intelligent 360° cameras
  • Pan-Tilt-Zoom (PTZ) cameras
  • AI-powered tabletop cameras

Some models use AI to track and zoom in on whoever is speaking. That’s useful for remote participants, though it can distract people in the room if the images are projected live on a big screen.

Personal preference matters too. Your setup should let participants opt in or out of camera use.

They may feel certain cameras are invasive, or they may need to limit camera use while sharing sensitive information.

You want each person to feel comfortable and in control of their environment.

Here are three brands known for high-definition cameras:

  1. Logitech Rally Camera: A PTZ camera with Ultra-HD imaging, 15x HD zoom, and a wide field of view. It’s built for professional video conferencing, with smooth pan, tilt, and zoom plus Logitech RightSense technologies for automatic framing and light adjustment.
  2. Cisco TelePresence SpeakerTrack 60: A dual-camera system that uses facial recognition and voice triangulation to track and frame active speakers, with smooth transitions between them.
  3. AVer CAM540: A 4K PTZ camera with 16x total zoom (12x optical) and an 86-degree field of view. It uses SmartFrame technology for automatic participant framing and works with common conferencing platforms.

Conference room displays

Large screens are standard in most conference rooms. They used to be just for presentations or video clips. Now they also show everyone in a meeting, including remote participants, while discussions are underway.

There are several options for these screens:

  • Large-screen television or monitor
  • Projectors (using a plain white wall or drop-down screen)
  • LED video wall

These tools sit at the center of conference and meeting rooms and get used constantly.

Here are three brands known for conference room displays:

  1. Samsung Flip 2: An interactive digital flipchart for collaborative meetings. It has UHD resolution, touch capability, and easy connectivity, and lets multiple users write and draw at once, which suits brainstorming and presentations.
  2. LG 86TR3BF-B: An 86-inch UHD interactive board with multi-touch, supporting up to 20 simultaneous touch points. It offers strong image quality, a clear interface, and compatibility with common collaboration software.
  3. BenQ RP8602: An 86-inch 4K UHD interactive flat panel for corporate use. It has advanced touch, built-in collaboration tools, and eye-care features to reduce strain during long sessions. It supports wireless screen sharing and comes with a whiteboard app.

Meeting room booking system

A meeting room booking system makes reserving rooms simpler and prevents double bookings and scheduling conflicts.

It makes room availability clear, so teams can plan and coordinate. It also helps make sure meeting spaces get used well.

In short, they matter.

  • Add meeting services such as catering, room setup, and layout changes. Read more about that feature here.
  • Invite everyone to join onsite to boost collaboration
  • Improve your meeting rooms based on usage data
  • Book from anywhere on a visual floorplan

Meeting room displays

Often the last piece of business in a meeting is picking a date and time for the next one with the same group.

Meeting room displays usually extend a booking system, showing room availability in real time. That lets people set a date and reserve the same room for a future meeting.

Attendees can also check the meeting room display before each meeting to confirm they’re in the right place.

OfficeRnD Workplace offers meeting room displays that improve visibility, cut booking confusion, and integrate with Outlook and Google.

How to choose the right technology for a hybrid workplace

When it comes to choice, you need to know the best conference room technology for you.

Think ahead as you invest. Voice recognition and AI-assisted meeting tools are now common in conference rooms, and AI camera framing and noise reduction are becoming standard features. Watch for those.

Each facility also has site-specific factors, including:

  • Security
  • Privacy laws
  • Acoustics

The exact mix of technologies and products is up to you. Balance your budget against what your users actually need.

If you’re a facility manager, consult your clients directly to get their input. Real client data beats guessing at what they want.

Choosing the right conference room technology for a hybrid workplace means weighing a few factors so communication and collaboration hold up for both in-person and remote participants. With most remote-capable employees now working hybrid or fully remote, conference rooms need technology that supports people wherever they join from.

Assess your needs

Start by understanding your team’s needs. Look at the types of meetings you typically hold, whether small huddles, large presentations, or brainstorming sessions. Count participants, in-person and remote, and consider how much interaction each meeting needs.

Audio quality

Clear audio is essential. Choose microphones that capture voices accurately and cut background noise. Ceiling and boundary array microphones from Shure and Audio-Technica are strong choices. Make sure your system includes reliable speakers for clear sound output.

Interactive displays

Interactive displays support collaboration by letting participants share and annotate content in real time. Displays like the Samsung Flip 2 or the LG 86TR3BF-B offer touch and high-resolution screens that keep meetings productive.

Unified communication platforms

Pick a communication platform that ties video, audio, and collaboration tools together. Microsoft Teams, Zoom, and Cisco Webex all support meetings that mix in-person and remote attendees.

Ease of use and integration

Make sure the technology works with your existing systems and is easy to use. Complicated setups slow people down and cause frustration. Favor solutions that require little technical expertise to operate.

Room to grow

Think about how the technology grows with you. As your team expands, your conference room setup should handle more users and adapt to new needs. Modular systems make that easier.

Weigh these factors carefully and you can pick conference room technology that supports collaboration, hybrid work, and productivity.

Best practices for setting up new technology

Buying and installing conference room technology isn’t plug-and-play. Setting it up for your facility can get complicated.

Here are a few things to keep in mind:

Optimize the room layout and acoustics

For the best audio and visual experience, pay attention to the room’s layout and acoustics.

There are four things to consider:

  • Focal point: Use flexible furniture and arrange seating so participants can turn to face a central point or large screen when they need to.
  • Speakers: Place speakers throughout the room for even sound distribution.
  • Acoustics: Use acoustic panels or carpets to absorb sound and reduce noise for participants.
  • Visibility: Make sure everyone can see all screens or whiteboards by simply turning their chairs.

Set up strong security and data protection

Companies need to feel their confidential information is safe at your facility.

How much security you need depends on how sensitive the information is and who your clients are. All companies are bound by at least some data privacy rules.

Here are several security measures to have on hand:

  • Use keycard or biometric access for conference rooms
  • Encrypt data shared in the facility
  • Install privacy filters on the windows

How to get more from your conference room equipment

Upgrading an existing or new facility isn’t cheap. To get a solid return, understand what your target clients or team members want. Survey users or analyze data on how your facilities are being used.

New technology is also often misunderstood. It can be misused or broken if people don’t know how to use it.

Part of your job as facilities manager is to train staff on the technology you install. Staff should also keep up with the latest conference room technology trends.

The communal kitchen can provide a valuable gathering spot for members to take a break. It allows them to relax and refuel without leaving the office and breaking their work stride.

High-Quality Air and Lighting

Good air circulation and plentiful natural light are crucial for creating a comfortable and healthy work environment. Paying attention to these factors can reduce fatigue and boost the moods of your members.

They’re a great option for members who require confidentiality or want to avoid the background noise of communal areas. Mail and Package Handling

A dedicated mailroom for receiving and sending packages adds a layer of convenience for members, especially those running their own small businesses. This service ensures members never miss important deliveries and can manage their correspondence efficiently.

6 Unique Amenities to Help a Coworking Space Stand Out

The fixtures discussed in the last section are basic services you’ll need to provide as a coworking space provider; any coworking spot worth its salt will have them. If you want to stand out to your potential clients, though, you’ll need to go a step further.

Green spaces

Either way, these features could boost the appeal and marketing potential of a coworking space. Plus, these green areas could provide locations for local sustainability initiatives, such as recycling drives.

Virtual Reality (VR) Lounge

A VR lounge equipped with the latest virtual reality technology can offer an escape from the ordinary, allowing members to engage in everything from virtual meetings and design work to meditation and stress relief. From Tenants to Community: Building Connections Through Amenities

In coworking spaces, amenities go beyond mere conveniences; they act as catalysts for community building and fostering connections among tenants. By making your space a hub for relaxing, socializing, and networking — as well as just a place to work — you can offer your members a sense of community that makes their monthly subscription fee well worth the continued investment.

Moreover, hosting events and workshops catering to the interests and needs of the members can further cement the community feeling. These can range from professional development seminars and networking mixers to wellness activities and social gatherings.
