Name: Exceeding Expectations: How To Wow Customers [12 Key Tips]
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: Mediocrity is everywhere.
Post body:
Mediocrity is everywhere.

Even companies with the best intentions rarely get past bland, run-of-the-mill customer service, whether their customers are other businesses or the public at large.

Plenty of companies are comfortable there. They deliver what they promise and build a customer base over time. To stand out and grow, though, you have to exceed expectations.

Quick Summary:

This article covers what it takes to go beyond the basics and stand out with exceptional customer service. We’ll look at:

  • Why exceeding expectations is a strong tool for customer retention
  • 12 strategies for exceeding customer expectations, including going the extra mile, connecting authentically, and personalizing your customer interactions
  • Examples of companies that impressed their customers by exceeding expectations

What does “exceeded expectations” mean?

Exceeding expectations means doing more than what someone expects you to do. In customer service, it means delivering an experience that goes past the quality, speed, or care a customer assumed they’d get.

Meeting expectations is not the same as exceeding them. When customers expect a certain quality of a product or service, they expect the provider to meet that bar.

Companies that meet expectations keep a good standing in the market. Those that consistently beat them are the ones that stand out.

Whether your customers are private consumers or other businesses, leaving them with exceeded expectations builds customer retention, brand loyalty, and word-of-mouth marketing.

12 key principles of exceeding expectations in business, with examples

Regularly exceeding expectations sounds like a tall order, but it isn’t impossible. There are solid principles companies can build into their core values and daily practices.

Here are 12 principles of exceeding expectations, with examples of how different companies have put them into practice.

1. Going the extra mile

Going the extra mile starts with going beyond basic requirements to offer unexpected extras.

If you’ve ever bought a new car and then received a box of cookies in the mail from the dealer, you know how that small touch can make you think more highly of the dealership.

The same holds true in a remote or hybrid environment. An employee at a far-away location who goes out of their way to solve a customer’s problem, even if it means staying up late in their timezone, can turn a one-time customer into a regular.

Getting better-than-average service tends to produce a pleasant sense of surprise. When customers feel valued instead of taken for granted, they’re more loyal to the company.

Example: Ritz-Carlton

Luxury hotel chain Ritz-Carlton is known for its customer service. Its staff is trained to anticipate and fulfill guests’ wishes, whatever they might be.

More than that, each employee can spend as much as $2,000 per guest, per incident, to solve a problem, without a manager’s preapproval. In practice, staff rarely spend anywhere near that. The point is the freedom to act on the spot.

2. Connecting authentically with your customers

Trust and rapport keep customers coming back. In Salesforce’s State of the Connected Customer, 88% of customers said the experience a company provides is as important as its products or services, the highest that figure has ever been.

To connect authentically, invite open feedback and actually listen, through surveys or by emailing or calling customers to hear their comments. Those feedback loops help you tailor what you offer to what customers need.

Example: Zappos

Footwear and apparel company Zappos, which consistently scores high in customer satisfaction, asks for customer feedback continuously.

Their website includes a “Your Voice Matters” section inviting shoppers to share their experience, followed by a survey with meaningful questions. The honest feedback guides the company as it improves its service.

3. Personalizing your customer interactions

Personalizing your customer interactions makes customers feel valued. It means tailoring experiences to individual preferences and customizing how you communicate.

Greeting your most valued customers by name leaves a lasting impression, whether it’s the cashier at the local grocery store or the finance director at a multinational you do business with.

Online, this means personalized messages and recommendations that make customers feel like more than an anonymous face in the crowd.

Example: Netflix

Netflix personalizes customer interactions by analyzing user data to provide customized content recommendations.

From personalized homepage selections to tailored show suggestions, the company makes each user’s viewing experience unique.

4. Prioritizing quality in product or service delivery

Speed matters as a business metric, but rushing to hit quotas or deadlines shouldn’t come before the quality of the product or service.

“Quality over speed” is a strong retention mechanism. A cup of coffee handed to you in under a minute won’t impress you if it tastes like it’s been sitting in the pot for hours.

You’re far less likely to return to that shop than if your latte had been made properly, even if it took five minutes.

Example: Apple

Known for its attention to detail and commitment to quality, Apple leaves no gap in its product development process.

Apple’s focus on quality runs from its choice of materials to its user interface. The result is products that set industry benchmarks.

5. Using technology for personalization

Data technology may seem far from day-to-day customer interactions, but it’s a strong ally for a better experience. Data analytics gives you insight into customer preferences and behaviors, so you can personalize interactions at scale.

By the way, you should also gather and analyze data related to your workplace so you can make more informed business decisions. OfficeRnD Workplace’s Workplace Analytics lets you do just that.

AI and machine learning can push personalization further by making accurate recommendations based on past interactions, giving customers experiences that fit them.

Example: Spotify

Spotify commits to personalization through its curated playlists and music discovery algorithms.

These introduce users to new music and adapt to their listening history. The result is an individualized music experience.

6. Providing human interaction in customer support

Customers value having real people available by phone or live chat, and that value is easy to underestimate.

AI has raised the bar rather than removed the need for it. In Zendesk’s CX Trends 2026 report, 74% of customers said it’s frustrating to tell their story over and over to different agents. People want to be recognized and helped without starting from scratch.

Companies meet customer expectations by setting up effective communication systems. They exceed them by reaching out immediately to customers who have left messages, addressing them by name, and showing they care.

Example: American Express

American Express provides 24/7 customer support by phone and chat, so help is available whenever it’s needed.

The company makes the point playfully on its website: “When we say we’re here for you, we mean it. Our ‘office hours’ never end, so you can get in touch with us 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. (Yes, you can speak with an actual human.)”

7. Handling mistakes gracefully

Mistakes in business are inevitable. How you respond to them defines your reputation.

For hybrid or remote employees who don’t meet customers face-to-face, it can be tempting to ignore mistakes and leave people hanging. Customers are used to being treated this way.

That’s why remote and hybrid workers who take customer experience seriously can shift a company’s reputation for service.

Acknowledging errors, taking responsibility, and offering a genuine apology can turn a negative experience into a positive one, especially when you add a real solution and fair compensation.

Example: Southwest Airlines

Southwest handles mistakes well. It’s quick to acknowledge disruptions, whether that’s a delayed flight, mishandled baggage, or something else, and it apologizes to affected passengers.

When serious issues occur, Southwest offers solutions such as rebooking on the next available flight, providing compensation or vouchers, and looking after passengers during long waits.

8. Empowering your team to deliver exceptional customer service

Empowering employees to take ownership of customer interactions pays off when it comes to exceeding expectations.

Well-trained team members create a culture of service, trust, and autonomy. Encouraging autonomy and creativity leads to better solutions and better service.

This isn’t limited to in-person work. With the right tools, hybrid and remote teams can work together to provide top-tier customer service.

OfficeRnD Workplace is workplace management software that helps hybrid teams coordinate in-office time in one place. For example, it has a set of collaborative scheduling features that let employees plan in-person days for team work and collaboration.

Example: Disney

This anecdote shows how far Disney employees will go for guests.

12-year-old Brooklyn lost her talking teddy bear, Toby, at Disney World. The bear, which she’d owned since she was three, was a gift from her father, a soldier who had since lost his life, so she was devastated when it disappeared.

After much searching, cast members at Disney’s Saratoga Springs Resort found the teddy bear and mailed it back. When the box arrived, it also held a photo album of Toby at special Disney spots, including with Winnie the Pooh.

9. Providing proactive customer support

Staying a step ahead of your customers’ needs and resolving problems before they escalate is a mark of exceptional service. Proactive support means anticipating issues and offering solutions before customers ask.

Example: Amazon

Amazon does this well with its shipping notifications. By keeping customers informed about order status at every step, Amazon cuts the need for delivery inquiries.

10. Offering a generous return policy

A generous return policy shows a company’s commitment to customer satisfaction. It allows returns for defects, dissatisfaction, or a simple change of mind.

By reducing friction in the return process, companies turn negative experiences into positive ones.

Example: Costco

Wholesale club Costco is a prime example of a generous return policy. It lets customers return products with minimal hassle and usually without an explanation.

That approach is a big part of Costco’s reputation for customer loyalty.

11. Under-promising and over-delivering

Exceeding customer expectations often starts with setting realistic ones and being transparent about what customers can expect.

From there, going beyond what you promised creates the “wow” factor. Doing it consistently is what builds brand loyalty.

Example: Tesla

Tesla built a reputation for exceeding expectations by delivering electric vehicles (EVs) that go beyond industry norms.

Tesla vehicles sometimes provide more real-world mileage per charge than the EPA-rated figure. A Model 3 may list an estimated range, but drivers often report squeezing out a bit more.

Under-promising and over-delivering has helped Tesla build a base of passionate owners who stay loyal to the brand.

12. Delivering consistency across channels

Consistency is the base of a strong brand experience. When a company keeps things uniform across every touchpoint, whatever the location or platform, customers always know what to expect. That builds familiarity and trust.

Example: Starbucks

Starbucks keeps its branding consistent. Whether you’re in-store, using the app, or in the loyalty program, the brand experience stays uniform. That consistency helps customers feel at home with the brand however they engage with it.

Name: Setting Fail-Proof Time Management Goals [Examples & Tips]
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: Proper time management is a skill — and just like any other learned skill, it takes patience and practice to become a master of it.
Post body:
Proper time management is a skill — and just like any other learned skill, it takes patience and practice to become a master of it.

In this article, we’ll show you how to create realistic and impactful time management goals that will help you boost your productivity and improve your focus.

Quick Summary:

Time management goals are specific objectives that managers and employees can put in place to improve their use of time and enhance their productivity. They can include strategies for:

  • Prioritizing tasks
  • Minimizing distractions
  • Setting realistic deadlines

Time management is a soft skill that requires practice and deliberate action to execute. It comes naturally to some people but requires dedication for most others.

Setting realistic time management goals is the key to accomplishing them. It’s also essential to understand your personal work ethic, along with that of your team members to ensure these goals are achievable.

What Are Time Management Goals?

Time management goals are targets for improving your task management both at work and in your everyday life.

Both employees and employers can use time management goals to help reduce procrastination, set achievable deadlines, and establish routines to boost their productivity.

An employee, for instance, could set a personal time management goal to complete all their major tasks by 3 p.m. daily.

A manager’s goal could be to delegate responsibilities for upcoming assignments within the first two days of getting briefed on those assignments.

According to recent research, the core essentials of time management include the following:

  1. Effective planning
  2. Setting goals and objectives
  3. Establishing deadlines
  4. Delegating responsibilities
  5. Embracing new learning opportunities
  6. Eliminating distractions
  7. Forecasting

When your team has a clear understanding of their time management goals, their task distribution, efficiency rates, and morale will often improve.

Time management goals don’t just apply to in-office workers, either — they’re also relevant to hybrid workplaces. For teams with flexible working arrangements, keeping all employees on time with their task completion can help improve the organization’s efficiency and workload management as a whole.

An example of a time management goal in a hybrid workplace could be for all team members to respond to each work email they receive within 24 hours. This will help them maintain effective communication channels and task coordination throughout the work week.

Why Are Time Management Goals Beneficial?

Time management goals aid in tracking progress and provide a framework through which to effectively identify areas that need improvement in workflows and routines.

Without them, asking employees to manage their time is a bit like putting them in the middle of a complex maze with no map and expecting them to easily find their own way out.

Time management goals also provide managers with valuable insights into workplace management and how their team operates within time constraints.

Other time management goal benefits include the following:

  • Improved and measurable productivity rates
  • Reduced stress levels
  • Enhanced focus and longer-lasting periods of deep work
  • Better work-life balance
  • More effective task achievement

It’s important to recognize that time management doesn’t just come naturally to all employees and that every single member of your team has a different level of proficiency in this area. This will help you get the most out of your team as a manager.

Therefore, tailored and realistic time management goals that help guide and support employees lead to improved productivity and job satisfaction. These goals should be customized to meet employees at their current skill level and help them both achieve their larger career goals and meet their daily work deadlines.

Time Management Goal Examples for the Workplace

Time management is commonly considered a soft skill in the workplace — a routine that employees often figure out on their own as they advance through their careers or pick up by observing others.

However, the misconception that time management will naturally develop over time with no assistance can be detrimental to a team’s effectiveness, particularly in the context of hybrid work.

Time management is a habit that requires deliberate attention, refinement, and effort to master. As such, it leans closer to a skill than a character trait.

Time management goals shouldn’t be “set-it-and-forget-it” tasks nor approached with a “one-size-fits-all” mentality. It’s crucial to regularly review and adjust each of your team members’ time management systems to ensure they remain effective and relevant.

Below are some detailed examples of constructive time management goals for the workplace. Notice how they’re presented in a manner that’s supportive and respectful instead of overwhelming, belittling, or patronizing.

Time Management Goals for Employees vs Managers

Time management goals for employees and managers should look different to account for the different responsibilities these individuals have in their work lives.

While managers oversee entire teams, employees focus on individual tasks and, therefore, concentrate on their own performance rather than that of their colleagues.

Example 1: Employee

“Spend 30 minutes each Friday afternoon organizing my weekly schedule for the following week using a productivity planner.”

Example 2: Manager

“Delegate responsibilities to my team members based on their strengths and respective workload capacities. Organize regular check-ins to provide guidance and support, and allocate enough time for strategic planning and team development to help my employees through their assignments.”

Time Management Goal Examples for Employees Who Struggle With Procrastination

Employees’ struggles with procrastination stem from both external factors, like distractions and mobile phone use, and internal factors, such as perfectionism, a lack of self-regulation, and low self-efficiency.

Setting time management goals for employees who struggle with this issue can help keep them level-headed. When crafting these goals, focus on well-researched strategies that involve short bursts of deep work, such as the Pomodoro Technique. Managers should understand, though, that micromanaging their employees is a bad managerial technique.

Example 1

“Utilize the Pomodoro Technique to work in focused 25-minute intervals, followed by 5-minute breaks, to maintain concentration and combat my tendency to procrastinate during the day.”

Example 2

“Complete at least one high-priority task before checking my emails or engaging in non-essential activities within the first 2 hours of my work day.”

Time Management Goal Examples for Employees Who Struggle With Meeting Deadlines

Meeting deadlines is particularly challenging for offices that deal with client-facing work and tight schedules.

Time management goals can help employees effectively prioritize their tasks, allocate adequate time for each element of an assignment, and minimize the need to rush or request an extension.

These kinds of time management goals should be specific and highly achievable to help employees stay organized and focused.

Example 1

“When I’m assigned a large project, I will use a notepad to break the task into smaller, manageable sections with individual deadlines. This will help me meet the final project deadline.”

Example 2

“I will utilize a task management tool and my Google Calendar to time block specific time slots for each task that I receive throughout my work week.”

Time Management Goal Examples for Employees Who Struggle With Prioritization

Some employees find it difficult to identify which task is the most important in their work stack, leading to emphasis being placed on assignments that may not be as important to the company as others.

The fact is that productivity and efficiency suffer when teams are scattered and disorganized with their time. Because we have limited capacity in our work weeks, goal-driven prioritization is essential to remembering and executing important tasks.

Set time management goals that establish clear priorities for employees. For example, categorizing tasks into quadrants using the Eisenhower Matrix can help your employees prioritize their work time.

Example 1

“I will use the Eisenhower Matrix to categorize tasks that I receive over the next month based on their urgency and importance, as well as ensure that only two to three tasks are put in the ‘Urgent and Important’ column.”

Example 2

“I will allocate 30 minutes at the beginning of each day to identify and rank tasks that I have scheduled based on their impact and deadlines so that I know which tasks I should work on first.”

Time Management Goal Examples for Employees Who Struggle With Setting Achievable Goals

Some employees struggle with saying “yes” to every task or request to please their managers. While this may seem harmless, time is an employee’s most valuable resource. Therefore, if they continue giving it away without considering their schedule, overcommitment and low productivity can result.

To help address this, managers can help employees set achievable time management goals.

Example 1

“I will break down long-term projects into smaller steps and, if needed, ask for help to complete tasks on time.”

Example 2

“I will set a maximum number of tasks to complete each day based on my available time and resources.”

5 Tips for Setting Time Management Goals

Setting time management goals might appear easy at first; however, it can be challenging to implement a strategy that both works and ensures team morale stays high.

When setting time management goals, managers need to be both assertive in setting clear expectations and considerate of their employees’ feelings.

While you might have the best intentions for improvement, coming across as overly critical can make your employees feel like the work they’re doing isn’t good enough or undervalued.

Here are some tips that’ll help strike the right balance.

#1 Implement the “2-Minute Rule”

The “2-minute rule” is a time management technique that involves completing any task that can be done in 2 minutes immediately rather than postponing it.

Employees and managers can use this tactic to:

  • Respond to short emails or messages immediately to prevent them from piling up and causing delays
  • Complete quick admin tasks, such as updating records

For instance, an employee could file an important document right away instead of delegating it to a colleague or delaying it.

#2 Use Time Blocking to Set Realistic Goals

Time blocking involves scheduling specific blocks of time in a calendar or productivity tool rather than writing a to-do list.

Employees and managers can use this tactic to:

  • Set aside specific time blocks throughout the day for deep work on complex tasks
  • Schedule meetings and video conferences at one consistent time slot during the day to help avoid distractions

For instance, a manager could block off 2 to 4 p.m. every Tuesday to give their employees planning and analysis feedback.

#3 Make Use of the “Ideal Me” vs “Worst Me” Technique

The “ideal me” vs “worst me” technique involves listing what you’d ideally want to achieve in a day followed by the “worst” version of tasks — and then finding a realistic middle ground.

Employees and managers can use this tactic to:

  • Help individuals identify recurring behaviors holding them back from success
  • Serve as a moderator for setting realistic goals

For instance, an employee may aim to complete five major tasks in a day as the “ideal me” scenario, while the “worst me” scenario involves completing only one task and procrastinating for the rest of the day. Therefore, a realistic goal for this individual would be to complete three tasks during the day.

#4 Conduct a Personal Time Audit

A personal time audit involves critically tracking and analyzing how you spend your time during your work hours, typically by writing down your hourly activities and achievements on a notepad, in a time-tracking spreadsheet, or using a time-tracking tool.

Employees and managers can use this tactic to:

  • Help determine and overcome the pitfalls in your time management technique
  • Perform a weekly review to examine how close you’re to achieving your time management goals

For instance, after conducting a personal time audit, an employee might find they’re wasting time constantly checking their email inbox throughout the day. They might then decide to designate a maximum of 10 minutes for this task daily.

#5 Practice the “Eat the Frog” Philosophy

The “Eat the Frog” method of working was developed by Brian Tracy. It involves tackling the most challenging and important task first thing in the morning to increase productivity and reduce procrastination.

Employees and managers can use this tactic to:

  • Build momentum for the day and reduce the tendency to procrastinate on challenging assignments
  • Prioritize important tasks

For instance, a manager might schedule a stand-up meeting for their entire team as the first task of the day.

In addition, watch this short video below that demonstrates a very efficient time management technique.

Start Setting Realistic Time Management Goals

Time management goals only work if those goals are realistic and achievable.

While having ambitious aspirations for how you want to spend your time is a good thing, without a proper plan in place, your chances of success can decrease.

The key to success is to understand your own work ethic, strengths, and preferences, as well as what motivates you to remain focused and productive.

Keep in mind that no two people are the same — you have to find what works for you and your team.

Name: 7 Tips To Build A Successful Coworking Business In 2025
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: Building a successful coworking brand is challenging. This business has the physical limitations of real estate, the unpredictability of a high-velocity business, and the complexity of a hospitality company.
Post body:
Building a successful coworking brand is challenging. This business has the physical limitations of real estate, the unpredictability of a high-velocity business, and the complexity of a hospitality company.

It can serve many customers, from individual freelancers to the largest global enterprises. It’s also a complicated community-building exercise that involves creating an environment where all these customers can work together.

In addition to that complexity, 2024 was the fourth year since the perfect storm, which unleashed unprecedented office utilization challenges, high inflation, super-high interest rates, and a completely unpredictable business climate.

Yet, the best coworking brands are thriving! They have done a lot of things right. We studied hundreds of coworking and flex space businesses and found the top 7 traits of the most successful brands—the ones with the highest occupancy rates, the best retention rates, growth, and profitability.

Let’s dive in.

#1 Define a Clear Ideal Customer Profile (ICP)

The best coworking brands have an extremely well-defined Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) down to the smallest detail. Some target VC-funded, seed-stage tech startups with 3-20 employees, while others focus on mid-aged, successful solopreneurs working in creative industries.

The ideal customer profile defines your most valuable potential customers’ firmographic, environmental, and behavioral attributes. It is developed through both qualitative and quantitative analyses. You can read more about it and follow a well-established framework by Gartner here.

The ICP aligns marketing, sales, service, and executive teams with the highest-value customers. It also focuses on scalable and repeatable strategies and tactics to engage and convert top accounts. Finally, it drives target account list creation, segmentation, organizational structure, and other key activities!

Having a very clear ICP in coworking is essential because, as mentioned above, potentially everyone can be your customer – from a freelancer to a multinational corporation.

You don’t want to waste time on the wrong customers instead of chasing more of the right customers. Having more of your best customers (and less of your worst) will help with retention, occupancy rates, growth, profitability, product offering, and everything in between!

You can start building your ICP by:

  1. Creating a unified spreadsheet with all the data you can collect for your existing members.
  2. Talk to your customers and try to learn as much about them and their decision-making as possible.
  3. Analyze the results and build assumptions.
  4. Validate and iterate until you feel you nailed it by observing!
Pro tip: Try to estimate the size of your market based on the ICP. Are there enough of your perfect customers in the area?

Knowing your best customer (ICP) will allow you to polish and perfect your best product further. We discuss creating an ideal customer profile in our extensive guide on SEO for coworking spaces.

#2 Have a Hero Product

The best and most successful coworking space companies we have evaluated have a standout product. They are famous for that one specific product, which helps them sell more of their other products.

For example, some spaces offer the best event spaces in town, which will help them sell more desks and offices. Others offer the best day passes in the city.

As a result, they can more easily sell their offices and meeting spaces. Some have outstanding designs and character for their buildings, and others have an incredible community.

Of course, your killer product can offer all services at the best price.

Your Ideal customer profile (ICP) should be able to easily connect your brand to your hero product or feature of your space! Everything gets so much easier after that.

Interested in further learning what makes a coworking space business successful in 2024 and beyond? Don't miss checking out the trend-setting webinar of the year!

#3 Win the Local Market

The most successful coworking spaces win their local markets first! They usually saturate their small town or city well before expanding to other cities, states, or countries.

Almost all great brands start by winning their local markets, opening three to five or more locations in a city, and completely dominating it before they move on.

The power law applies very well here – the dominating brands in a local market get the majority of the opportunities.

Researching our customer base shows that having more locations in a city increases the lead flow exponentially.

In difficult times, the best strategy is to focus! Focus on your core market and win it! If you cannot do it alone, you can always hire a coworking consultant to help you out.

And here, you can learn more about the current state of the coworking space industry.

#4 Go Small-town or Suburban

It’s no secret that the Central Business District and the Financial Districts struggle the most in the post-pandemic world. However, the Suburban spaces have been doing very well lately!

These are both very good reasons to expand in small towns. However, the main reason is that you will inevitably have less competition in the early days and will be closer to where people live.

All research out there is pointing out that the main reason for people to work from home is not that they don’t like the office in general. Or that they like working from home so much.

The problem is that people hate the commute. People hate spending hours in their cars.

So, if your coworking space is near your ideal customer profile’s home – you have a win and a much better chance to convert them to customers.

2025 will be the year of small-town and suburban locations. Still, here’s a great guide on what to consider if you’re looking to start an urban coworking space.

#5 Just be Profitable

I know it sounds easier than it is. However, in 2025, you have to be profitable. The best brands out there are profitable. Some of the best-performing coworking space operators are generating a 20% EBITDA margin on an individual location basis.

This is a very healthy margin for a hospitality business. It’s challenging, but it’s doable.

  • Increase your topline by nailing your ICP, polishing your hero product, and winning your local market.
  • Improve the bottom line by renegotiating your base rent, finding operating efficiencies, utilizing AI in sales and marketing, investing in good tech, etc.

Coworking can be profitable!

#6 Sign Better Deals with Landlords

The physical location remains the most significant cost and crucial element of a coworking space, which will remain true in 2025.

There are many details to consider when signing a new contract with a landlord. Our research shows that the best brands are very good at negotiating great deals with their landlords. They usually align the incentives well and turn their landlord into a strong partner. Some of the critical elements of the contract include:

  1. Type of contract – management agreement vs. lease agreement or some form of hybrid.
  2. Specific terms for getting out of the contract—this is also a very important term, as some locations don’t work, and in that case, you should be able to shut them down.
  3. Fit-out and renovation costs—In many cases, you should be able to negotiate with the landlord how to share the costs of the fit-out and renovation of the flex space.

#7 Secure the Right Funding

2023 and 2024 were the worst years for funding any type of business. Hopefully, next year will be a little better.

There are different funding paths for coworking operating companies.

  • VC (Venture capital) – that’s arguably the worst funding for a coworking space. Almost all VC-backed coworking spaces failed, with WeWork and Knotel at the top. The main reason is that VC money is tied to high-growth, high-margin, mostly tech businesses. This is very hard to do in real estate or hospitality, quickly creating a significant misalignment between the company and the investor.
  • PE (Private Equity) – PEs can work better for coworking and flex spaces than VCs. There are many flavors of PEs; some can be more patient and support strong coworking operating companies.
  • Family Offices – Often, family offices can be a good investor in a coworking business. They can provide patient capital suitable for hospitality and real estate brands like coworking.
  • Local Councils – oftentimes, regional councils can provide additional funding to coworking spaces when they are opening locations in the local area. Many councils can recognize the massive splash effect of good coworking spaces on an area. So they are more and more willing to help fund new openings!
  • Debt – debt is always a good option to finance a profitable coworking operating business. 2023 and 2024 were hard and 2025 will likely be almost as hard; however, debt is always an option if you have good company!

When securing funding, the most important element is always to have a very good alignment between your business and the investor!

Building a thriving coworking business doesn’t have to be complicated. You need to be well-educated and plan for success.

Name: 15 Best Communication Practices For Hybrid Teams [2024]
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: For hybrid teams, miscommunication isn’t just a nuisance — it’s a barrier to success.
Post body:
For hybrid teams, miscommunication isn’t just a nuisance — it’s a barrier to success.

Misunderstood emails, unclear objectives, project delays, and conflict can quickly become a frustrating cycle, straining productivity.

But thankfully, there’s a better way to blend in-person and virtual interactions: using innovative communication practices specific to hybrid workplaces. In this article, we’ll offer you some novel, effective strategies for communication.

With this knowledge in hand, you can steer your team toward success.

Quick Summary:

  • Effective communication is the bedrock of business success.
  • Hybrid teams need to use modern and uniquely tailored communication practices to thrive.
  • Some of the best communication practices include developing communication personas, adopting asynchronous video updates, and gamifying communication training
  • Our list offers innovative and actionable communication practices that you can use right away.

What Are Communication Practices?

Communication practices are the methods and approaches to exchanging ideas or info within a team. It’s how we choose to speak and work together in the workplace.

When it comes to hybrid teams, these practices are even more crucial.

In the absence of face-to-face interactions, managers need a more deliberate approach to communicating. Here, digital tools aren’t just conveniences — they’re lifelines.

An effective communication strategy relies on:

  • Clarity
  • Empathy
  • Tech-savviness

Whether they’re hosting a meeting or sending out a project update, managers must ensure everyone on their team feels informed and connected without being overloaded.

The Importance of Effective Communication Practices on a Team

Now that we’ve covered what communication practices are, let’s learn why they are so vital to teams.

Brings the Team Together

Whether work is remote or in-person, thoughtful communication creates belonging and unity. It helps establish an ideal environment for a group to become a team.

Communication also acknowledges each team member’s contributions and helps the team understand the company’s values.

Gallup has found that many managers aren’t ensuring healthy communication among their teams. And that’s not good for employee engagement or, ultimately, retention.

Communication is the glue that brings your team together — and keeps them there. That’s why mastering effective team coordination is so important.

Drives Productivity

Without clear communication, especially in hybrid environments, misunderstandings can plague a team.

Good communication streamlines processes and keeps workflows efficient.

In fact, project managers report that communication is one of the top skills in meeting objectives since it helps businesses achieve their goals, keep their projects on the right course, and maintain their budgets.

A hybrid team with clear task assignments and regular status updates is more likely to stay on track than one that doesn’t have these things.

Evolves Your Business

Sidestepping the pitfalls of poor communication frees your team up to evolve with agility. As a result, they can work together more effectively while embracing new tech and trends.

With effective workplace communication, challenges are seen as opportunities for innovation and learning.

15 Best Communication Practices for Hybrid Teams

Now, let’s get into the nitty-gritty. The communication practices below are vital to a hybrid team’s success.

#1 Assess Your Team’s Communication Styles

Understanding each team member’s communication style is very helpful, as it allows you to tailor your communication to their strengths. This helps everyone feel heard and understood, and it also reduces misunderstandings.

Simple assessments can help you gather this information.

#2 Develop Communication Personas

Once you know your communication styles, take it one step further by developing fictional personas that represent them. Use these in training sessions to help your team members understand and adapt to each other.

This is a great exercise that teaches a deeper understanding of the many ways people process and share information. As a result, it’ll strengthen your team dynamics.

#3 Integrate Silence in Meetings

Amazon is well-known for starting meetings by having everyone silently read a detailed memo. This puts everyone on the same page to contribute more thoughtfully.

With everyone absorbing and reflecting on the same information, holding discussions and making decisions becomes easier.

#4 Adopt Asynchronous Video Updates

Short video messages sharing project updates or feedback are a great way for hybrid teams to communicate better. They combine the personal touch of face-to-face communication with the convenience of text.

These updates are an engaging way to get around the scheduling conflicts that often come with in-person meetings and real-time collaboration.

Interested in learning more about working asynchronously? Here’s a great guide on mastering asynchronous communication and another one on conducting asynchronous meetings effectively.

#5 Practice Reflective Listening (Even When Virtual)

Reflective listening is always important, but even more so in virtual communications.

Train your team to not only hear but also understand and reflect on what is being communicated. This means summarizing and paraphrasing what others say.

Active listening helps to prevent misunderstandings and difficult situations and pushes the conversation to a higher level of engagement.

#6 Gamify Communication Training

Games aren’t just for play — they’re a big part of how we learn.

Add gamified elements to your communication training. For example, allow team members to earn badges for resolving conflicts or hold awards ceremonies to acknowledge top communicators.

These approaches make learning more engaging and encourage communication skill development in a fun and interactive way.

#7 Introduce Communication Health Checks

Anonymous surveys can offer a glimpse into how communication is going within your team. Think of these as communication health checks.

Share your findings with your team, and brainstorm together on areas of improvement.

Communication health checks are good for short-term fixes. They help to create a culture where open dialogue and communication are valued.

#8 Leverage AI-Powered Tools

Another great way to gauge the quality of communication in your team is through AI tools. These can analyze communication patterns and offer insights into where communication can improve.

For example, these tools may detect:

  • Employees who tend to dominate the conversation
  • Employees who need to be encouraged to contribute
  • Long email response times
  • The tone and sentiment within communications

With this information, you can make sure all voices are being represented — and help prevent future conflicts as a result.

#9 Establish “No Interruption” Hours

“No interruption” hours are times when no team meetings are scheduled, and employees are encouraged to focus on deep work. This practice respects individual working styles and rhythms and helps reduce digital fatigue and burnout.

With dedicated time for productivity, your staff can work without distractions.

#10 Establish a Virtual “Water Cooler”

Just as in-person teams have the physical water cooler, remote teams need an online space to gather and have casual conversations.

This virtual space is for bonding over non-work-related topics, and it’s crucial for team morale and unity. For hybrid operations, they’re a vital way to create shared spaces for connection.

#11 Practice Reverse Mentoring

Reverse mentoring programs pair senior team members with their junior colleagues. Veterans have a great deal of experience and knowledge to share.

However, reverse mentoring allows younger team members to share their perspectives, enthusiasm, or knowledge of tech or trends with senior staff.

This practice strengthens the intergenerational relationships on your team and boosts communication and mutual understanding as a whole.

#12 Level Up on Virtual Feedback

Feedback is an opportunity. Quality feedback is actionable, specific, and well-balanced, establishing harmony between positive reinforcement and constructive criticism.

Such an approach in virtual performance reviews creates a supportive atmosphere — one that encourages growth in a motivating environment.

#13 Hold Emotion Check-ins

Begin each meeting with a brief check-in where team members can share the mood or emotion they’re currently experiencing.

This practice cultivates emotional intelligence among team members. It builds empathy and an environment where staff members understand each other.

Because hybrid setups can’t rely on the same level of body language and eye contact, directly acknowledging the human aspect of work can be powerful for communication.

#14 Encourage Microlearning

Microlearning modules are short training exercises on specific skills. Having them available to your team lets them develop communication skills at their own pace.

This flexible approach is particularly suitable for hybrid teams, as it accommodates different schedules and learning styles, and it allows team members to work on their communication skills without overwhelming their workload.

#15 Organize Cross-Cultural Workshops

A cross-cultural workforce is becoming the standard for hybrid teams. Host workshops that focus on communicating across cultures. They should educate team members on different communication norms and styles.

Such training reduces misunderstandings and enables a more respectful work environment.

Name: 8 Real Virtual Team Challenges And How To Overcome Them
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: If you manage a remote or hybrid workforce, then you’ve probably hit some roadblocks at some point on your journey.
Post body:
If you manage a remote or hybrid workforce, then you’ve probably hit some roadblocks at some point on your journey.

Communication can be tricky, especially if you’re juggling multiple time zones with a mix of remote and hybrid workers. Establishing a thriving office culture while maintaining productivity is another common challenge.

But don’t throw in the towel just yet. This post will address some of the most common virtual team challenges and offer clear, actionable strategies for overcoming them that you can implement today.

Quick Summary:

  • Virtual employees commonly face challenges related to communication, office culture, trust, distractions, resources, productivity, security, and the employee experience.
  • While these challenges may seem daunting, they don’t have to be. There are actionable ways to address each of them.
  • Learn how to support your virtual team through challenges to create a work culture that supports effectiveness and productivity.

The Growth of Virtual Teams

Virtual teams have been around since the late 1990s, with the introduction of the Internet. While some companies embraced them early on, others saw a dramatic increase during the pandemic.

While virtual employees can be fully remote, more and more companies are embracing a hybrid model in which employees come into the office some days and work remotely on others.

Globally, 39% of knowledge workers are hybrid, while 9% are remote.

Virtual work is a win-win since companies can pursue the best talent out there when they’re not limited by geography, and flexible schedules give remote employees a better work-life balance.

Remote teams don’t typically experience losses in productivity, either. In fact, about 31% of team leaders report improved productivity as a result of shifting to hybrid work.

Despite these benefits, virtual teams come with some challenges. Here are just a few of them and some resolutions.

8 Challenges of Virtual Teams (Plus Solution Tips)

#1 Communication Issues

Communication is a commonly cited challenge among virtual teams. Communication difficulties include response delays, working with people in multiple time zones, and limited collaboration time.

In addition, there are no opportunities for “watercooler” connections when teams work remotely. Plus, many nonverbal cue challenges require attention too.

Tips for Overcoming Communication Challenges

Establish consistent communication channels and ensure that each team member has access to them. You’ll need platforms for video conferencing, holding larger team meetings (including back-to-back ones), and scheduling 1:1 check-ins.

While email is optimal for formal communications, encourage informal social interactions through channels like Slack or Teams.

Also, encourage and provide opportunities for team member collaboration. Even employees who are motivated to share knowledge enjoy boosts in creativity.

The use of a collaborative scheduling platform can make this even easier. Your team members can customize invites and send them to their teammates. Hybrid workers can also check to see who’ll be in the office on the same days as them to arrange meet-ups.

Finally, get your team members on the same page despite time zone differences by identifying common meeting times.

You may want to alternate meeting days or times each month so that everyone has opportunities to participate. Here’s a useful guide on conducting successful asynchronous meetings.

And don’t forget to determine appropriate response times for emails and informal chats.

Interested in learning more? Check out this guide on the most effective communication practices as of 2024.

#2 Office Culture Could be Jeopardized

Developing a strong office culture is another challenge virtual teams often face since not everyone on a team works in the office at the same time — or even at all.

Tips for Overcoming Office Culture Challenges

Address your office culture through team building, having a shared mission, and making informal connections.

First, ensure your employees know the company’s mission, values, and collective goals.

Consider incorporating virtual team-building activities into your routine to boost morale and strengthen company culture.

These activities can range from a low-key shared virtual lunch to a fun-filled murder mystery for your employees to solve. Get everyone’s input, and add the events to the shared calendar.

You can also help your employees build connections through icebreaker activities, which you can use to kick off your virtual meetings or schedule into informal chats every week.

#3 Trust

Trust is crucial for encouraging employee engagement, but it’s often a challenge for virtual teams.

That’s primarily due to the lack of face-to-face interaction and physical presence, which are often key in building interpersonal relationships and mutual understanding.

Without the nuances of in-person communication, such as body language and immediate feedback, it can be more difficult to establish and maintain trust.

Plus, remote work environments can sometimes lead to feelings of isolation or out-of-sight, out-of-mind concerns, making it challenging for team members to feel fully connected and confident in their colleagues’ commitments and contributions.

Tips for Overcoming Trust Challenges

First, make the company’s processes, roles, and employee responsibilities transparent for all employees. Post any relevant information in shared folders for easy access.

Ensure each employee’s role is clearly outlined each time a project is kicked off so you can address concerns or frustrations immediately.

Remember those communication channels?

Encourage your employees to reach out with their questions and concerns by upholding an open-door policy. Tell your employees when they should expect a response and who they can contact if you’re out of the office.

#4 Distractions

Multi-tasking during virtual meetings, response delays, and adjusting to various environments are common distractions remote teams face.

Tips for Overcoming Distraction Challenges

While you may be unable to eliminate distractions, several tactics may help your employees avoid them.

Start by identifying potential barriers to your employees’ workdays. What are the most frequent distractions they face? Brainstorm solutions with them and follow up regularly.

Establish clear meeting guidelines to reduce multi-tasking or response delays, including whether employees need to have their cameras on. Assign employees different roles, such as timekeepers and note-takers, during your meetings to keep them on track.

Use shared tools to set goals and milestones, give other members progress reports, and convey expectations.

#5 Lack of Resources

Virtual teams can also face resource challenges, especially when there’s no office space to pick up supplies or check on equitable distribution across geographical locations.

Furthermore, remote workers might face difficulties in obtaining immediate support or troubleshooting technical issues, which can impede their productivity and efficiency.

Tips for Overcoming Resource Challenges

Your best bet for overcoming resource challenges is to ensure your employees have equal access to the resources they need to perform their jobs.

Offer stipends or allowances for them to purchase the necessary tools. Provide information and training on problem-solving technological or other issues as needed.

#6 Productivity

Productivity can be challenging among virtual teams when employees have difficulty adhering to deadlines and completing their projects on time. Not to mention that the lack of in-person collaboration is a menace to employee productivity.

Tips for Overcoming Productivity Challenges

Set clear long-term goals and short-term objectives. Ensure your employees are aware of important deadlines and how they relate to the company mission.

Get in the habit of developing SMART goals — goals that are strategic, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound — every time. This will help provide clear direction for all team members.

Review time management strategies with your team and offer training if needed. Popular methods include time blocking, to-do lists, “Eat the Frog,” and the Eisenhower Matrix.

Set clear deadlines, and outline how your team members will be held accountable for projects.

OfficeRnD Workplace software helps you create clear policies and enables employee presence tracking to help boost productivity. And it can do a lot more.

#7 Security Concerns

Security poses unique remote and hybrid work challenges, too. With the increased use of personal devices and a wider variety of locations employees can work from, the need to maintain safety in and out of the office is heightened.

Tips for Overcoming Security Challenges

Start by ensuring your current practices are secure. Your technology should be robust, and employee training should be consistent.

Follow up regularly on safety and security practices, and post your policies and resources in easily accessible shared spaces.

Offer accessible channels for employees to report safety concerns, and commit to proactively responding. If you operate a hybrid workspace, employ a visitor management system to keep your employees safe while they’re in the office.

#8 Employee Experience Issues

A positive employee experience is crucial to retaining top talent. This challenge is particularly nuanced in virtual teams, where creating a cohesive and engaging work environment remotely can be challenging.

The absence of physical interaction and office dynamics can lead to a sense of disconnection and isolation among team members, impacting their overall job satisfaction and engagement.

To add more, maintaining a healthy work-life balance can be more complex in a remote setting, where the boundaries between personal and professional life are often blurred, potentially leading to burnout and decreased morale.

Tips for Overcoming Employee Experience Challenges

Focus on the entire experience, from onboarding to offboarding. Your employees should feel supported and encouraged from the moment they join your company.

Additionally, promote a positive work-life balance among your employees. Hybrid and remote workers may struggle to establish clear boundaries if their laptops are always accessible. Teach your employees the signs of burnout, and provide support when needed.

Keeping your employees engaged will help to reduce their overall stress levels, leading to a more positive experience while on the job.

Some companies even go a step further and hire a dedicated employee experience manager.

Leveraging Technology for Enhanced Virtual Team Collaboration

In the evolving landscape of remote work, technology plays a pivotal role in bridging the gap between virtual teams.

By harnessing the right tools and platforms, organizations can significantly enhance collaboration, streamline communication, and boost overall productivity. Here’s how.

Choosing the Right Collaboration Tools

Selecting the right set of tools is crucial for virtual team success. Tools like Slack for communication, Trello for project management, and Google Drive for file sharing are indispensable.

They provide a centralized platform for team interactions, ensuring that everyone is on the same page.

In addition, using hybrid work software that has collaborative scheduling abilities can help. For example, OfficeRnD Workplace’s rich set of collaborative features allows you to see who’s in the office on any given day and book a desk next to your favorite colleague. That impacts in-person collaboration and productivity.

Integrating AI and Automation

Artificial Intelligence (AI) and automation are game-changers in managing routine tasks. AI-driven chatbots can handle basic inquiries, schedule meetings, and even provide project updates, freeing up valuable time for team members to focus on more complex tasks.

Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR) in Workspaces

The use of VR and AR is revolutionizing remote collaboration. These technologies create immersive virtual environments that mimic physical office spaces, allowing for more interactive and engaging team meetings and brainstorming sessions.

For example, the virtual collaboration platform Orbital.chat whose popularity grew by 9200% between July 2023 and September 2023, offers enhanced user experiences and innovative functionalities through an immersive virtual experience.

Data Security in Virtual Collaboration

With the shift to digital platforms, data security is paramount. Implementing robust encryption for communications and ensuring that cloud storage solutions are secure can protect sensitive information from unauthorized access.

Training and Skill Development

Equipping team members with the necessary skills to utilize these technologies effectively is crucial. Regular training sessions and updates on the latest digital tools can enhance team efficiency and adaptability.

While addressing these challenges may take time, the payoff will be substantial.

You’ll see gains in office culture, communication, and trust. This will lead to a better employee experience, resulting in improved productivity and profitability for your business.

Using the right tools is crucial for that.

Name: Mastering Asynchronous Meetings In 2024 [An Expert Guide]
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: Online meetings are commonplace these days. Many employees are comfortable meeting via apps like Zoom, Skype, or Google Meet.
Post body:
Online meetings are commonplace these days. Many employees are comfortable meeting via apps like Zoom, Skype, or Google Meet.

But what if your colleagues span multiple time zones, including regions on the other side of the world?

In this case, face-to-face interactions are typically not an option. Alternatives for the meeting organizer include doing all business via email or instant messaging — or conducting an asynchronous meeting.

An asynchronous or “async” meeting may sound like an oxymoron, but we’ll explain how technology can host productive remote meetings online without requiring everyone’s presence at the same time.

Quick Summary:

  • An asynchronous meeting is a collaborative process where participants engage and contribute at different times, rather than meeting simultaneously.
  • Asynchronous meetings have distinct benefits compared to real-time meetings.
  • However, there are also some drawbacks.
  • This article covers five best practices and eight detailed facilitation steps for the most productive, collaborative async meetings possible.

What Is an Asynchronous Meeting?

An asynchronous meeting is a meeting in which the participants do not interact in real time. Instead, they engage with their teams at their convenience, primarily through written communication, still trying to follow proper meeting room etiquette.

Though async meetings are becoming more popular, one-third of company leaders have never heard of them.

The flexible approach asynchronous communication offers makes it possible for remote and hybrid work teams to have productive, effective meetings.

Organizing asynchronous meetings is complex. Unlike traditional online meetings, where everyone gathers in the same virtual space simultaneously, asynchronous meetings require certain skills and strategies. We’ll discuss a number of these below.

But first, a few reflections on the benefits and drawbacks of async meetings.

The Pros and Cons of Asynchronous Meetings

Asynchronous meetings come with a set of advantages and disadvantages. Let’s discuss a few of each.

Pros

The advantages of async meetings include the following:

  1. They open the door to wider global collaboration than standard online meetings. Specifically, they offer more personal flexibility since participants can choose to engage when it best suits their schedule.
  2. The flexibility async meetings offer can improve hybrid workers’ work-life balance. Workers who are spread across the world don’t have to get up very early or stay up late to catch important meetings.
  3. Async meetings can potentially generate higher-quality participation since the participants have time to think through their contributions. They can come up with questions before the meeting to share with their teammates.

Cons

The challenges of asynchronous meetings include the following:

  1. Communication delays and missed deadlines can happen due to communication not occurring in real-time.
  2. Some participants may find it difficult to stay engaged with the meeting topic in the course of a long, drawn-out conversation.
  3. Participants must have effective written communication skills to address issues and opinions clearly and succinctly.
  4. These meetings can be mismanaged and become unproductive as a result.

With these pros and cons in mind, let’s look at how to maximize the benefits of asynchronous meetings while minimizing their drawbacks — beginning with best practices.

Best Practices for Asynchronous Meetings

To make asynchronous meetings work follow the best practices described below.

1. Set Company Policies and Guidelines

At the policy level, set (or request from HR) company-wide policies and guidelines for asynchronous meetings to avoid confusion among the participants and keep everyone on the same page.

These policies should include expectations for participation, response times, and the tools or platforms to be used in these formal company meetings.

2. Select Suitable Communication Tools

Choose reliable communication and collaboration tools that support asynchronous meetings. Think of email threads, project management software, or dedicated platforms like Slack or Microsoft Teams. Here’s an extensive list of some popular collaboration tools.

Ensure that all necessary individuals have access to the chosen communication tools, and, if necessary, provide them with training on using the software’s key features. Make sure everyone is comfortable with the technology.

Here’s a great guide on the best communication practices for 2024.

3. Be Mindful of Time Zone Implications

When scheduling deadlines, consider the range of time zones you’re dealing with, and make sure to accommodate participants from different regions.

You could do this by providing a reasonable window for contributions. Time zone conversion tools can help you find suitable meeting windows.

4. Respect Flexibility

Since async meetings can span several days, prepare for unforeseen challenges or delays in contributions by having a backup plan.

An example of such a hiccup is one or more participants being confronted with unexpectedly busy schedules and having difficulty getting back to the discussion thread in the async communications.

The backup plan could include solutions such as shortening or extending the meeting timeframe or taking some discussion components offline.

5. Ask for Extra Documentation

Since team members aren’t in the same room at the same time in an async environment, it’s easy to lose track of discussion threads and decisions. Participating in back-to-back meetings further amplifies this.

To support this, invest some time in thorough meeting documentation. Encourage participants to create meeting notes and summarize discussions, decisions, and action items to create a clear record of the meeting proceedings.

How to Conduct an Effective Asynchronous Meeting: 8 Tips

Running a successful asynchronous meeting involves some well-defined strategies. Here are eight steps and tips for meeting facilitators to make these team meetings interesting and productive.

1. Set Clear Meeting Objectives

Start with a well-defined meeting goal and a clear agenda to keep the event focused and manageable.

Next, specify the time frame for the meeting. For instance, “This meeting will take place over three days, from Tuesday at 9:00 AM ET through Thursday at 5:00 PM ET.

Send out these details and any relevant documents ahead of time to ensure that all participants know the purpose and dates of the meeting.

It’s helpful to create a consistent communication schedule for updating participants on the progress of the meeting. For instance, you could plan on sending out a progress report at the end of each half-day session.

2. Clearly Define Your Participation Expectations

Clearly articulate the participation level you expect. For example: “We’ll have three discussion rounds. I’d like everyone to contribute at least three ideas, suggestions, or questions in each round. Also, everyone should comment on two posts from other team members.”

Also, encourage the participants to communicate concisely and avoid unnecessary jargon, abbreviations, side comments, etc. Explain that these practices promote clarity so that their async conversations will be easily understood.

3. Use Effective Engagement Strategies

Keep the participants involved and engaged by posing questions, initiating new discussions, and encouraging them to comment on each other’s contributions. Use mentions or tags to notify specific individuals when their input is needed.

Another effective engagement tool is to assign responsibilities for meeting components. For instance, one person can keep a log of the decisions made, another can lead a discussion on a subtopic, and a third can summarize key points.

Lastly, encourage constructive feedback. Create a climate where participants can openly discuss the meeting’s progress, suggest improvements, and address any challenges that may affect the desired outcomes.

4. Monitor Participation

Make sure that all team members contribute regularly. If some participants are lagging in responding, gently remind them or provide additional context to help them further.

5. Use Recordings

Consider recording key discussions or summaries to keep participants on track and help latecomers catch up. Make these recordings easily accessible for reference.

6. Summarize Key Points and Action Items

Periodically summarize key points, decisions, and action items.

Share these with the participants in chats, or post them in a designated work folder that’s accessible to everyone. This will help to keep everyone informed on the meeting’s progress and outcomes. Some tools can help you document meetings quickly. Check out our article for the best hybrid meeting equipment for more info.

7. Document the Meeting

Keep a well-organized folder of meeting documentation items, including meeting agendas, summaries, action item lists, and feedback records. Important recordings can also be archived there.

Access to this archive should be readily available to the team members as long as the team is working on that specific project.

8. Regularly Evaluate Each Meeting’s Effectiveness

It’s good practice to periodically gather feedback on your async meetings to evaluate their effectiveness — and use this information to make continuous improvements.

By following these hands-on steps and tips, you can facilitate asynchronous meetings that are engaging, productive, and instrumental for meaningful collaboration.
