Name: How Hybrid Work Can Increase Business For Your Flex Space
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: Hybrid work is now the default for most knowledge workers, and that steady demand for flexible, on-demand space is one of the clearest growth opportunities in front of flex operators today.
Post body:
Hybrid work is now the default for most knowledge workers, and that steady demand for flexible, on-demand space is one of the clearest growth opportunities in front of flex operators today.

A flex space is a shared, professionally managed workspace that companies and individuals rent on flexible terms, by the hour, day, week, or month, instead of signing a long commercial lease.

Hybrid work used to be a perk you found at startups and tech companies. It has since become standard. The now and the future of work.

That shift is good news for the flex space industry. JLL projects that 30% of all office space will be consumed flexibly by 2030, and corporate demand is the fastest-growing part of the market.

To answer the question of how you capture that demand, we invited our friends at Deskpass, a platform that offers as-needed access to an ever-growing network of professionally managed workspaces.

By working with thousands of spaces worldwide they’ve been closely observing the current dynamics and have valuable insights to share.

Find them below.

Written by Megan Eileen McDonough, Community Director at Deskpass

The debate over returning to the office is largely settled, and hybrid is the model most companies landed on. For flex operators, that means a steady stream of new audiences to reach, if you know where to look.

We’ve outlined four ways that hybrid work can bring more business to your flex space, plus tips for getting eyes on your product.

How does hybrid work bring in more members?

Companies have moved from allowing occasional remote work to building hybrid into how they operate, and many need space their employees can use a few days a week without a fixed lease.

The appetite is real. In a study by WeWork and Workplace Intelligence, 64% of employees said they would personally pay for access to an office space, and 75% would give up at least one benefit or perk for the freedom to choose their work environment. 76% of the C-Suite said they were likely to give employees a stipend to work from home or a coworking space.

Those stipends are how a lot of hybrid workers end up at your door. We’ve heard from our partner spaces that companies are providing stipends starting at around $200 per month to be spent on day passes and up to $500 per month to go toward dedicated desks or small offices. Prepare for those employees and focus on attracting them (more on that later).

How can you meet evolving demand?

Joining a network like Deskpass is a good first step to being seen. To take it further, make sure your flex space offers a unique experience others in your area don’t.

Deskpass makes this easy, with filters like Women-Owned, BIPOC-Owned, Mother’s Room, Standing Desks and Outdoor Space to select and display on your profile (find more about the benefits of Deskpass at the end of this article).

We’ve rounded up ways flex spaces can prepare for the wave of remote workers, because ready or not, here they come. Many companies run “virtual first,” meaning employees work from home or a workspace of their choosing. For flex spaces, that means larger companies may start using your space too.

One way to appeal to companies in your area is to reach out directly and ask how they’re solving for remote and hybrid work. You might also update your marketing to speak to these companies. Redesigning your space to meet the needs of new members, and potentially turning large offices into brainstorming or training rooms, are other steps you can take to meet this demand.

That midweek surge is worth planning around. CBRE’s 2025 Americas Office Occupier Sentiment Survey found that 73% of occupiers reached full capacity on peak days, while only 34% did so on average days. Tuesday through Thursday fills up while Mondays and Fridays stay quiet, so price and program accordingly.

Keyless entry is another selling point, especially with many remote workers wanting 24/7 access to work during their most productive hours. Think about the touch-points a person has when accessing and using your space. Can you make entering the building, unlocking an office, and getting to work easier?

Finally, flexibility. Workers want it, and a lot of it. For many companies that means monthly terms instead of longer ones, renting private offices by the day, or new part-time memberships.

On Deskpass, we’ve noticed a large increase in demand for private offices by the day or week, and for the ability to have employees visit multiple flex spaces within 5 miles of their home.

How does hybrid work support a diverse community?

One of the biggest advantages of a hybrid model is a wider, more diverse talent pool. Hybrid work helps companies recruit top talent and keep them happy. Talent is everywhere, even halfway around the world.

Location bias matters less. Many of the most desirable companies to work for have offices in expensive markets. A hybrid model widens the talent pool to different locations, economic backgrounds, cultures and skill sets.

Diversifying your team brings other benefits, like new ideas and exposure to other cultures. Working with people from different backgrounds gives you perspective on different working environments and cultural norms.

As a flex operator, prioritizing diversity is one way to attract new members and get them excited about joining a supportive community.

How Deskpass can help you drive more business

Hybrid work opens your doors to larger companies. When a company gets familiar with a space, it’s easier for them to picture that space in their team’s future. The move to flex is often gradual before it becomes permanent. The first step is getting decision makers through your doors.

Joining a network like Deskpass gives you instant access to people looking for a place to work in your city. Deskpass is a Work From Anywhere solution for companies with remote or distributed teams. Through their network of thousands of workspaces, they provide on-demand desks, meeting rooms and private offices by the hour, day, week and month.

Deskpass connects your flex space with people looking for a place to work. There are three types of Deskpass members: those who day-hop, those who work at companies with a remote or hybrid model, and teams looking for in-person meeting rooms or private offices.

Instead of paying extra to advertise, listing your space on the Deskpass network is free and lets workers in your area easily reserve a hot desk, meeting room or private office. As a space on the network, you get paid for every reservation made through Deskpass.

Operators on the Deskpass network cite brand awareness, more members, and the ability to show the product to prospective clients as reasons for joining. It can also convert members. As one space manager explains, “Deskpass has positively impacted our operations by bringing in a variety of potential members to try out our space. They see the value we offer to our members and then convert to our platform.”

Turning new demand into recurring revenue

Getting hybrid workers through the door is the start. Keeping them, and billing them without manual work, is where operators either scale or stall.

That’s the operational side of capturing hybrid demand. Day passes, part-time memberships, stipend-backed bookings, and multi-location access all add complexity to billing, access control, and reporting. Handling that by hand doesn’t hold up once volume picks up.

OfficeRnD Flex is space management software for coworking and flex spaces that automates member onboarding, bookings, and billing from one place. It handles member lifecycle management, automated billing and payments, booking and reservation management, and analytics, with over 50 native integrations for payments, accounting, door access, and Wi-Fi. For operators running more than one location, it gives a single view of resources, occupancy, and revenue across the whole portfolio.

The AI Hub inside OfficeRnD Flex adds an AI Sales Agent that responds to every lead instantly, around the clock, across chat and email. When a hybrid worker or a company’s facilities lead reaches out about space, they get an answer without your team stopping what they’re doing.

Name: The Success Stories of 250 Coworking Spaces Around the World
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: We believe the global coworking community is what creates more success stories of coworking spaces. And we’re always glad to put a spotlight on meaningful projects worth sharing.
Post body:
We believe the global coworking community is what creates more success stories of coworking spaces. And we’re always glad to put a spotlight on meaningful projects worth sharing.

Back in early 2021, we sat down with Coworkies co-founders Pauline Roussel and Dimitar Inchev. They’d just finished their book, “Around The World in 250 Coworking Spaces,” and we wanted to spread the word about it.

“Around The World in 250 Coworking Spaces” is a printed book of curated coworking stories that documents how founders start, grow, and run flexible workspaces around the world, told through the people, spaces, and communities behind them.

The book covers people, workspaces and products that shaped the coworking industry, and gives a picture of the diversity that exists across modern workspaces. It reads as a guide to how people start and build new work environments through collaboration, interior design and community activities.

We talked with Pauline and Dimitar about the book, the pandemic, and the power of community. Here’s our chat.

And if you want to learn more about successful coworking spaces, check the 4 Pillars of Successful Coworking Spaces blog post.

Hi Pauline and Dimitar, can you guys start by introducing yourselves?

Greetings to all of the readers. We are Pauline and Dimitar, Co-Founders of Coworkies. We are a French and Bulgarian who met in a coworking space in Berlin in 2015. Since then we work together on multiple projects, mostly related to coworking.

These projects gravitate around jobs in coworking spaces, how to have better communities and sustainability for workplace communities. While doing this, we travel extensively around the globe to meet the people who are building the world of coworking.

At the time of this interview, we’d visited more than 420 coworking spaces in 47 cities. Spinning from New York to Tokyo, and the many places in between.

And just for the record, there is no such thing as “best coworking space”. Each space is different and suits the needs of a specific customer. As we like to say, coworking is the same dish, each space cooks differently:)

What’s the “Around The World in 250 Coworking Spaces” book about and who is it for?

The book shares the stories of 250 coworking spaces from around the world. It’s a mix of answers of When, How, Why and for Who. The stories range from entrepreneurial journeys to the community needs to regional or city specifics.

We hope the book will give readers the opportunity to make their own journey (even through a book), find knowledge and inspiration and get a better understanding of what coworking really is.

We believe that there is no such thing as “the best coworking space”, without at least specifying for who and why. And we hope this book will help more people embrace this understanding.

The book is a good read for coworking space founders or people thinking of starting such a business. It’s also for anyone interested in flexible work environments: professionals involved in the future of work, community building, architecture, and real estate.

They will all gain a lot of knowledge from the personal stories shared in the book.

How did the idea of making a book come to life?

The idea for the book came from the coworking space founders and members we were meeting through the years.

We remember Tomas, architect and Founder of a coworking space called Based In, to be the first who suggested the idea. We were having a chat about his spaces and other spaces we’ve visited. He then said it would be a great idea to create a book that tells the stories of all these coworking spaces.

With time, we started to hear this from more and more people. Also, we started hosting private events called “Around the World of Coworking” in some of the spaces we were visiting.

Later on, in Mumbai, where we were visiting some coworking spaces, we finally decided to make it. We came up with the full name, and it clicked so well that it started our active work on the book, which took us 2 years.

Why did you decide to make a coffee table book and not a blog or an e-book?

This is a really good question and we had to answer it for ourselves before deciding to make the book. Our counter arguments were that we already have a blog and a magazine where we share openly about the people we meet, their spaces, and cities we visit.

So why make a physical book? The answer came from the fact that we are a very small team and we cannot compete with the big outlets online. So how do we make a difference? Coworking space teams are small, they have hundreds of tasks every day, and there’s a lot of online noise.

To reach them we had to do what no one else can, create a product that can be used offline in peace and in a calm state of mind. And that’s why we decided to make this coffee table book.

What useful insights can coworking operators find in the book?

It can give coworking space operators the sense of belonging; that they are not alone. They can learn from other operators across the globe how they deal with challenges and how they work through the day of a coworking space operator.

We’ve taken the #hashtag approach to help readers navigate through the book. So let’s say you are interested in “food” or “education”. You will be able to find the spaces falling into these categories, read their story and learn from their experience in making their space and community successful.

The business value is to create a global understanding that can be applied locally. To double down on that we’ve partnered with two global companies, the office furniture provider Kinnarps and access control provider Salto. They both helped us gain business insights from their case studies on how interior and technology can improve the member experience.

What are coworking operators doing to adapt to the new post-COVID-19 reality?

These were interesting times for the industry globally. When we spoke, the pandemic wasn’t over yet, but it also wasn’t “new” anymore. Spaces understood the challenges and knew what was needed to operate safely.

COVID-19 pushed operators to rethink their member experience within their facility. A lot of them invested in technologies of various kinds (from access control systems to air quality filters and more), adding more data to their spaces to operate with.

For many spaces, it became possible to know how many people are in the space, at any given time, and to monitor where they move around. Using data in coworking, coliving, and flexible workspaces more generally brings new opportunities to do things differently, with concrete numbers and metrics.

We also saw a shift in the way spaces manage their communities. Before the pandemic, most community activities were carried out offline. That changed, and spaces added digital tools to give members value whether they were present in the space or not.

That made coworking reachable from anywhere. Whether you are in Berlin right now and can access your space, or not, you can belong to that community and contribute to it. It also changed the level of memberships to include virtual options of different sorts (virtual office plans, virtual memberships, and more, Ed.)

The rise of remote work for larger companies was a big opportunity coworking spaces were ready to seize all over the world. Attracting a new kind of member, an employee from a larger company, brings novelty to the community as a whole.

It creates more work and learning opportunities for everyone, the new member and the existing ones. There are new community dynamics that spaces need to start thinking about.

Can you give us some COVID-19 highlights from the book?

When we started working on the book, COVID-19 was not on the world’s agenda. When the pandemic hit, we had to pause the project to see how each space we were featuring was adapting, shifting, rethinking its model.

We didn’t want the book to be all about COVID-19, but the pandemic had an impact on every space featured in it. Each space adapted differently because of a few factors:

  • Its locality: whether they are based in Asia, Africa, Europe, North or South America, COVID-19 hit everyone differently because of the time the virus reached them, and because of how their local government reacted (you can check the coworking industry report by CoworkIntel, Ed.). Which brings me to the second point.
  • Support from the local government: in certain parts of the world, flexible workspaces (including coworking, makerspaces, etc.) were recognized and supported by their governments and were asked to follow certain guidelines; in other countries, they were left in the middle, not exactly an office, not a hotel or a restaurant, and had to figure out what to do by themselves.

Those two factors shaped their response and transition as well.

  • Some of the spaces featured in the book told us COVID-19 helped them refocus. That term came up a lot in our conversations with them. Refocus of their space, their community, their business model, their marketing, and more.
  • With certain spaces, particularly makerspaces, COVID-19 brought a lot of opportunities. From printing face shields to launching online stores, full production lines, and more, makerspaces played a key role locally in many regions.
  • A lot of the spaces we featured received great support from their members in various ways, which was a good validation that their work was meaningful to many.
  • For a few, there was still a lot of uncertainty, mainly because their region was still heavily impacted or in lockdown.

What is the role of the community, the power of coworking, especially in times of COVID-19?

Community is key. The word has been overused, and frankly abused, in the last years. COVID-19 helped it heal. Many people understood the power of their community, how it helps them and why they need it.

As we started to say earlier in this interview, coworking spaces learned through the pandemic that managing a community doesn’t just happen offline anymore.

2020 taught everyone how to engage with members digitally, accepting that things are different and that members might not show up the same way they would if they were all in the same space.

But they do show up. At their own rhythm. Members embraced the digital space provided by coworking spaces to:

  • Motivate themselves to wake up and get dressed in the morning.
  • Find a new working rhythm, and know when to stop by attending an event at the end of the day to wrap things up with others, because when you work from home, it’s easier to work endlessly.
  • Take care of themselves through well-being events spaces organized. A lot of spaces told us members finally welcomed yoga or meditation during the pandemic because they needed something to help them stay calm and focused.

And yes, there might be zoom fatigue, or members might really want to go back to human contact and to their workplace. A space from the book told us members cried of happiness when they could go back there.

Somehow, everyone understood that navigating through COVID-19 is also a community effort. The more we follow the guidelines locally altogether, the faster we go out of this together.

Members embraced their communities in new ways, and spaces learned with them how to do that.

Where can people find the book?

The book started as a 30-day Kickstarter campaign, which the coworking and coliving community backed to bring the project to life. That campaign succeeded, and the book was printed and published.

“Around The World in 250 Coworking Spaces” is now available directly from the official book website. It’s a 352-page printed book covering 250 coworking spaces across 6 continents, with founder stories and 3 case studies on interior design, access control, and starting a coworking space. It sells for 79 EUR (about 85 USD), and each order includes a one-year subscription to the Coworkies Readers Club.
Meta title: The Stories of 250 Coworking Spaces Around the World
Meta description: Learn about Coworkies’ book about the success stories of coworking spaces. We also chatted about COVID-19 and the power of community.

Name: 2020 Year in Review – A Year to Remember!
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: 2020 was not the year we all at OfficeRnD expected! It was not the year we all anticipated!
Post body:
2020 was not the year we all at OfficeRnD expected! It was not the year we all anticipated!

This was a year when it felt like history was unfolding in real-time. Such turbulence is rarely pleasant to live through – we crave normality and a predictable pace of progress, and above all, we crave a sense of control over that progress.

The Covid-19 pandemic is a Black Swan event that redefined the world and will have an effect on every aspect of our lives for decades to come.

The speed of change in the real estate sector shifted gears and the adoption of new technologies and changing business models will happen in a much shorter period.

The world can no longer go back to long term leases, that’s for sure. The tenant-landlord relationship is changing faster than ever. Companies demand high-quality workspace service on flexible terms and no one can argue that anymore. In fact, many companies started asking the most fundamental question like, do we need an office at all? What is the future of office space?

Let’s go back to the basics and think about that for a moment.

Do we really?

Yes and No!

The future of the workspace

We don’t need a traditional static office in a crowded building.

Instead, we need an exciting, engaging space where we can meet and collaborate with our colleagues to make things happen, to bring new products to life faster! Name: 5 Benefits of Coworking Software For Your Workspace
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: The key benefits of coworking software are automated administrative tasks, improved operational efficiency, better member experience, a fully integrated technology stack, and visibility on key business metrics.
Post body:
The key benefits of coworking software are automated administrative tasks, improved operational efficiency, better member experience, a fully integrated technology stack, and visibility on key business metrics.

Coworking software is a management platform that automates the day-to-day operations of a flex space, from bookings and billing to memberships and reporting, in one system.

As a rule of thumb, the more you’re scaling, the more you can observe the positive impact of technology on your business. Because the more you are scaling, the more problems you face and the more your workload grows.

The market backs this up. There are roughly 42,000 coworking spaces worldwide as of the start of 2026, and operators are competing on how well they run, not just on desks and Wi-Fi.

But, before we move to what a management platform can bring to the table, let’s take a look at the following scenario. Does it sound familiar?

Your processes become more complex and clumsier day after day. Mundane, administrative tasks eat more and more of your workday while you have less and less time for strategic work. You keep working on growing your business but you feel kind of stuck.

At some point, it becomes difficult to keep track of data, memberships, bookings. You spend hours to export and import data from one system to another. Just to eventually find out that there’s a mistake in one of the sheets and you have to do this again…

Can this be different? Easier? More efficient?

It can.

A coworking software can help and below you will find out how.

1. Automates administrative tasks

Coworking software helps you automate a huge burden of your day to day activities. This includes but is not limited to invoicing, billing, contract and membership management, meeting room bookings.

Using a management platform removes the necessity to handle tens of spreadsheets and deal with mundane, repetitive tasks over and over again. Ultimately, this saves you hundreds of hours each month that you can dedicate to working on your strategy or finding new clients, for example.

A lot of spaces members use Google Calendar to book meeting rooms, for instance. Then, at the end of each month, they go in and manually count how many hours each company used and if they exceeded their allocated time. This eats a huge portion of their time and is also prone to errors.

A coworking software enables you to keep track of such data in the platform and automatically add it to the respective invoice at the end of the month. No need to manually review, count, or transfer data.

2. Improves your operational efficiency

What would your performance look like if you could decrease the time for a task to be done from 3 hours to 10 minutes, for example? A management platform will help you achieve this.

Automating and streamlining your processes enables you to do your work faster, more efficiently, and more precisely.

For instance, instead of spending 2 days to invoice all your members and send each member their invoice, you’d need 2 hours. Looking for proof? Common Desk, one of the most recognized flexible workspace brands with a network of locations across Texas and North Carolina, took their billing process to a whole new level by implementing coworking software – take a look at their story!

Increased efficiency means more value with fewer resources and input. And this will allow you to focus on other important processes like working on your strategy, selling more desks, etc.

For example, check out how OfficeRnD Flex has improved business for Downtown Works.

3. Improves member experience

Investing in a great customer experience definitely pays off! And, in coworking spaces, the level of customer experience is strictly related to how members interact with your space, amenities, and team.

Is it easy for them to book a room? How long does it take them to change their billing details? Is there a convenient way to submit a ticket?

You should always strive to make such processes as easy, convenient, and efficient as possible.

Another benefit of coworking software is that it can help you achieve this by:

  • enabling you to manage contracts and memberships so you can service your members fast and adequately
  • helping you keep track of membership-related data so you can easily access it when needed
  • providing your community with web and mobile apps to easily interact with your space, amenities, and team

This way, your members make the most out of your space. Ultimately, this improves customer satisfaction and loyalty.

4. Integrates and syncs all other systems and apps

Integrations enable clean, error-free data transfer from one system to another. This way, you don’t have to manually export, import, and transfer data from and to your apps and tools.

A lot of spaces use between 6 and 8 different tools to manage their operations and those tools are not connected to each other. This leads to lots of wasted time trying to synchronize data and huge chances for human error.

Probably, one of the most useful benefits of coworking software is that it can integrate and sync all other systems you use. These could be payment and accounting software, door access, WiFi, printing, and more.

For example, you can connect payment software like Stripe, and accounting software like Xero to your coworking software that will sync and automate the entire process. This will enable you to do a couple of things with just a couple of clicks: automatically generate and send invoices, collect payments, and update the data in your accounting tool.

5. Gives you visibility on key business metrics

Lack of visibility on key business metrics can not only prevent you from scaling but could be also harmful to your business.

It can lead to identifying critical problems too late, wasting valuable time to manually build key reports, and making inadequate budget decisions.

A coworking software enables you to tap into metrics such as occupancy, utilization, and revenue. It helps you reduce guesswork and rely on data for important decisions.

Should you invest in private offices? Are the meeting rooms on the 3rd floor regularly underutilized? What is your projected revenue for the next 6 months?

Data helps you find the answers to questions like these and ultimately make the right decisions. Here’s more on the topic of setting and measuring KPIs.

What about AI in coworking software?

The newest benefit worth watching is automation that goes past scheduled invoices and into your sales and support workflows. In OfficeRnD Flex, that layer is called AI Hub, and its first agent is an AI Sales Agent that responds to every inbound lead 24/7 across your website contact forms and shared inbox.

The problem it solves is timing, not lead quality. Someone fills out your contact form at 9 PM, your team gets to it the next morning, and by then the prospect has already toured another space. An always-on agent qualifies the inquiry, checks your availability and product catalog, and hands off warm leads to your team. For multi-location operators handling high inbound volume, that closes a gap no amount of manual follow-up fully covers.

6. Bonus tip: How to choose the best coworking software

If these benefits of using a coworking software already made you consider the option of investing in such a solution, it’s critical to find the right one for your space.

There are plenty of solutions on the market and the truth is there isn’t a one-size-fits-all solution. However, there’s a solution that fits your needs best.

To help you make the best choice, we’ve created a detailed guide on evaluating coworking software. We hope you’ll find it useful. 🙂

And if you want to make even more out of technology, don’t miss to check these top apps for coworking spaces. Combined with a coworking software, they make the perfect tech stack for your space.

Name: Enable Electronic Signatures For Your Coworking Space with OfficeRnD
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: Electronic signatures are standard now in coworking and flex spaces. Operators send lease and membership agreements for signing in a few clicks, and members sign from a phone before they ever set foot in the building. The benefits of going paperless go well beyond convenience.
Post body:
Electronic signatures are standard now in coworking and flex spaces. Operators send lease and membership agreements for signing in a few clicks, and members sign from a phone before they ever set foot in the building. The benefits of going paperless go well beyond convenience.

An electronic signature is a legally binding way to sign a document online from any device, with an audit trail that records who signed, when, and where. In a flex space, that means contracts get signed faster and stay organized in one place.

This post covers why electronic signatures matter for coworking operators, then walks through how to enable them in OfficeRnD Flex using our Dropbox Sign integration.

What are the benefits of electronic signatures for coworking spaces?

The main benefits of using electronic signatures in your space are faster contracts, stronger security, lower costs, and a better member experience. Dropbox Sign reports that contracts are signed up to 80% faster than paper-based ones.

Faster contract turnaround

Instead of chasing members around your space with a paper contract and waiting for it to come back, you email everything they need to sign. They can open, review, and sign whenever they can, from wherever they are: at your space, at home, in the gym. Same for you. Digitalizing the contract process makes it faster and more convenient for both sides.

Stronger security and a clear audit trail

Paper documents get damaged, lost, or seen by people who shouldn’t see them. Electronic signature solutions use strong encryption to keep documents secure. They also record who signed, when, and where, so you can track any changes made to the document. That audit trail matters for lease and license agreements, where you may need to prove intent and consent later.

Lower costs

Electronic signatures cut spending on paper, toner, packaging, shipping, and the physical space to store all those documents. Printing 20 pages only to catch a wrong number and reprint the lot is bad for your budget and the environment. Digital signing gives your staff back time they can spend on higher-value work, like following up on leads or selling desks.

Better member experience

Members notice the speed. Signing a contract electronically saves them time and effort, and turning a dull admin task into a couple of clicks improves how people feel about your space and your service.

Here’s how to enable electronic signatures in OfficeRnD Flex through the Dropbox Sign integration.

How to enable electronic signatures in OfficeRnD Flex

Step 1: Select your contract template

Imagine you have a client that is ready to move into an office. They have expressed interest over the phone and are ready to review the legal documentation and sign a contract agreement.

OfficeRnD Flex has three built-in contract types, and you can create your own. Navigate to Community / Contracts to create a new contract.

The Membership Agreement is more common in coworking and puts a framework and structure around the relationship between you and your members.

The License Agreement is built around the specific office provided to the customer. It originated in the UK serviced office industry and has stricter rules about its structure and the data it holds.

The Lease Agreement, also known as a tenancy or rental agreement, is usually signed between a tenant and a landlord. Broadly, it’s a contract between two parties, the lessor and the lessee. A lease agreement usually carries more legal consequences than the other two.

All of these templates can be customized. Contact us at support@officernd.com to tailor them to your design.

Step 2: Build the contract

For this example, we’ll create a lease agreement for the office. Select the “Add Contract” button and choose your contract type.

The contract will ask for a few key pieces of information:

  • Contact Company and Member Name
  • Contract Start Date and End Date
  • Specific Private Office
  • Deposit and Pricing
  • Additional Plans

You should also select the “Contract Terms” that will be included as legal verbiage within the contract. These documents can be created and modified in the “Terms and Conditions” section.

Once the details have been selected, click “Add” to create the contract.

Step 3: Generate the contract for eSign or PDF

After the contract has been created, click the cogwheel next to it to pull up quick actions. You can edit the contract, send it for eSign, generate a PDF, cancel, or delete it.

First, click “generate a PDF” to preview how the contract will look with the client’s information.

Once you’re happy with it, click “Send for eSign” to send the document to the customer.

eSignatures is a paid add-on in OfficeRnD Flex that the OfficeRnD team activates for you. Email support@officernd.com to request access. OfficeRnD charges a set amount per document sent, and the same charge applies to any contract you resend. You can track these charges under Settings > Account Details > Subscription Details.

Step 4: What the customer sees

Your customer Sarah gets an email with your branding letting her know a contract is ready to sign. She clicks the link in the email to sign the document.

The customer is guided through a series of prompts and asked to sign.

Step 5: Final contract and membership review

After Sarah signs, you get notified and are asked to sign from your end. As a rule, wait for the customer to sign their side before you sign as an admin, so you can still decline the contract if you need to make edits.

Once both parties have signed, the contract status becomes E-Signed and the member receives a “Contract Completed” email with a link to download the signed PDF.

You also get a notification that the contract stage changed, and the memberships are applied to the account.

That’s it. You’ve sent a document for eSign, collected a legally binding signature, and applied the membership without printing a page. If you have any questions about this process, reach out to support@officernd.com. We’re happy to help.

Name: How to Set and Track Coworking-Specific KPIs
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: The last quarter of the year is a great time for planning the next ahead – business strategy, budget, future projects, etc.
Post body:
The last quarter of the year is a great time for planning the next ahead – business strategy, budget, future projects, etc.

But to ensure you will be able to track and evaluate your business performance, you need to know your numbers. Or in other words – you need to define and set your key performance indicators (KPIs).

There’s still a lot of uncertainty for the future of coworking spaces but the COVID-19 crisis seems to be more understandable now.

The world is slowly going back (or moving forward) to the new normal.

We hope that the situation in your country has allowed you to start reopening your space and rebuilding your community. And also, to work on your strategy for 2021.

This article aims to help you do that by giving you more clarity about defining, setting, and tracking coworking-specific KPIs.

In the post, you will find:

  • What are KPIs and why do you need them
  • Some examples of coworking-specific KPIs
  • How to define and set your KPIs
  • How to measure KPIs within the OfficeRnD platform

We hope this is going to be helpful.

Let’s move on!

What are the KPIs?

A Key Performance Indicator (KPI) is a measurable metric that demonstrates business performance. It’s used to keep track of your progress towards a goal.

KPIs can be set on a high-level for the entire company or for each department of the organization – e.g. Sales, Operations, etc.

Why does your coworking space actually need KPIs?

Having KPIs allows you to follow strategic goals and reach your operation targets.

Moreover, it gives you the chance to monitor and measure your company’s health and progress. Also, it gives you access to data and allows you to analyze patterns over time.

Last but not least, implementing KPIs in your business routine helps you to solve problems more efficiently, make adjustments, and stay on track.

What KPIs are specific to coworking and flex spaces?

To bring more clarity around the essence of the KPIs, here are some examples of KPIs specific for coworking and flexible workspaces:

  • Increase the quarterly revenue target with 15%;
  • Double the number of members within a year;
  • Decrease the average number of churned members in the next 6 months;
  • Increase the average stay (retention) to minimum 1 year;
  • Triple the number of hotdesk memberships for the next quarter;
  • Keep stable the number of Private Office memberships;
  • Increase the membership prices with 5% in the next year;
  • Sustain an occupancy level of minimum 70%;
  • Maintain a minimum gap between resource and cash occupancy.
  • How to define the KPIs valid for your coworking business?

Start from your business model

Start from your business model and understand what your organizational objectives are. If you’re not sure where to start, discuss it with your teammates. You’re all in the same boat and everyone has something to share from their point of view.

Choose the main parameters you will be tracking

Pick a handful and don’t go too wild. If you choose too many parameters it will be hard for you to track and then analyze them. Better pick 4 or 5 and break them down into sub-parameters.

Set targets for each parameter

Set these targets based on the desired outcome. Of course, keep the things real and don’t put targets that are way beyond the capacity of your business.

Delegate responsibilities within your team

If your team is big enough, perhaps each person will be in charge of 1 single parameter. If your team is relatively small, try to logically group the parameters. This way, your teammates can more easily have control over them.

Set periods to review the performance

You can do that on a monthly, quarterly, or yearly basis, or combined. You can review and adjust the sub-parameters on a monthly basis. On the other hand, the bigger, strategic KPIs can be discussed on a quarterly or yearly basis.

Embrace the idea that this is an iterative process

Every KPI is a subject of change – either you haven’t defined the KPI correctly and you need to adjust it. Or maybe the environment has changed and you need to adapt to it – this is all part of the flow.

Bonus tip: Remember – your KPIs should be SMART. SMART stands for Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic, and Time-targeted.

How to track KPIs within the OfficeRnD platform

Set KPIs targets

In order to properly track your KPIs and data in the OfficeRnD coworking software, you need to ensure a couple of system settings are in line with your goals.

  • Upload all resources available in your space. The inventory or the available resources of your coworking/flex office space should be uploaded under the Space module.
  • While adding your resources, define monthly revenue targets for each desk, office, or custom resource. The target you are adding on a resource level will be used for calculating your Cash occupancy.
  • Configure your Revenue accounts. The system is distributing your revenue to 4 main Revenue Accounts. If you want to track the revenue streams of your business in more detail you can consider adding more revenue accounts and mapping the products and services you are offering to them.
  • Last but not least, the system allows you to set a “Hotdesk Coefficient” as we call it which actually defines how many memberships you expect to sell for each hotdesk.

Bonus tip: Analyze the market in your city and area and set prices that will be competitive and affordable. When setting up targets, take into account the best and worst revenue scenarios, as per the set prices, your current budget, rent, and building expenses. Set a specific period to reach your targets. Create a 2-year plan for price changes and growth.

Track Members’ Turnover

Usually, the basics of tracking members are related to New and Churned members but in the Members Dashboard you can also see information about:

  • Net New/Churned members – this is the difference between New and Churned members for the month.
  • Members Net Growth – it represents the number of Net New/Churned members as a percentage of the total Active members for the previous month. It is also a clear sign if you are growing in terms of members.

Comparing new and churned members gives you insights about the pain points where you need to put more efforts in:

  • If you don’t have a stable flow of new members each month – focus on your marketing and put efforts into attracting them.
  • If many members churn on a monthly basis, try to find out why. Organize short exit interviews, collect information from your current members, and conduct anonymous surveys. Work on improving the highlighted problem areas.
  • If your net members’ growth is negative this means that you have a tendency of losing members and difficulties in retaining them – focus on developing a retention program.

By exporting the Members report you can easily calculate the Members Retention Rate of your space (Active Members Current Month minus New Members Current Month) divided into Active Members Previous Month).

Comparing new members, churned members, and retention rate could give you insights about the pain points where you need to put more efforts in:

  • Analyze your retention rate and look for tendencies, such as seasoning, internal changes in the physical space, community, or team. Develop a retention program.
  • If your retention rate is below 100% but you have a positive Net Members Growth that might be a signal that you are doing well in terms of marketing and sales but you might think about improving the way you serve your customers. Retention Rate below 75% might be worrying.

Bonus tips:

  • A CRM integration, such as Hubspot, can help you keep your prospects in line.
  • With Zapier you can integrate your Mailchimp and keep members and prospects engaged.
  • Use the Collaboration section in OfficeRnD to support your retention efforts.

Analyze Revenue Data

The first thing you need to do is to set your resources and targets.

Then, to be aware of your Customers’ KPIs such as new, churned, and retained members.

Once you’re done with this, you can have a look at the revenue parameters and see how they relate to the desired state of your business.

  • The Memberships dashboard in OfficeRnD provides vital information about your performance in regards to Memberships, broken down by month. You can filter the report by location, plan type, group of plans, or by accounts.
  • To further analyze your Revenue you can use the Projected revenue dashboard and the Invoiced Revenue dashboard. The Projected Revenue report is showing your estimated revenue based on the Membership and One-Off fees that currently exist in your account. The Invoiced Revenue report calculates the revenue based on already invoiced Membership, Booking, and One-Off fees. It gives you the total invoiced revenue and the invoiced revenue per client.

Bonus tips

  • Have a look at the most and the least used memberships – this will give you ideas about how you can improve your business model and adjust the offered products and services.
  • Look into the already invoiced revenue and the upcoming projections – analyze the data and use it to identify potential revenue gaps.
  • Use a payment gateway to collect your payments quicker.
  • Export the Invoiced Revenue data and compare it with your projections.

Measure Occupancy & Utilization

Another parameter that you have to track in your space is your Efficiency. In order to do that you can bet on two main performance indicators – Occupancy and Resource utilization.

  • If the Workstation occupancy is much higher than the Cash occupancy that might be a signal that you are giving too high discounts.
  • Keep your occupancy high, but keep in mind that if you’re having a 100% occupancy this will not allow your members to grow within your space and might influence your retention rate.
  • Compare the revenue you generate per desk for all the resources and see which type brings you the highest revenue and focus on boosting this service further. Don’t forget to look into the occupancy of these resources – if it’s too low, then the price is maybe too high

Bonus tip: Look for tendencies. Analyze the resources that stay unoccupied for a longer period. Try to find a reason for that. Is it something with the setup of the office/the desk location (the light, the temperature, the furniture, the street noise)? Work from there for a day to find out. Consider adjusting the prices of these resources accordingly – this will increase your occupancy and will raise your monthly revenue.

Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: The OfficeRnD Member Portal is the branded web portal and mobile app where members of your coworking space book meeting rooms, pay invoices, view events, and manage their memberships. This guide walks through how to customize it so it matches your brand and gives members a reason to log in. There’s a video tutorial and step-by-step instructions below.
Post body:
The OfficeRnD Member Portal is the branded web portal and mobile app where members of your coworking space book meeting rooms, pay invoices, view events, and manage their memberships. This guide walks through how to customize it so it matches your brand and gives members a reason to log in. There’s a video tutorial and step-by-step instructions below.

The portal was built to carry your brand and show off the amenities of your space, so it’s worth spending an hour getting the details right.

Customize the OfficeRnD Member Portal video tutorial

How do you match the portal colors to your brand?

Once your Member Portal is active, matching the colors to your brand is the first thing to do.

First, upload an appropriate logo in Settings / My Account. Logos with a 4:1 ratio work best and scale correctly in the portal. Use a .png with a transparent background.

To adjust the colors, go to Settings > Experience Hub > Branding, turn on Customize, and pick your colors. Click View in Member Portal to preview the theme before you publish it, then Save Changes to apply. Any change you make here also applies to your Branded mobile app.

You can set three colors:

  • Primary Color is used for buttons and toggle switches, and it’s the color used in the mobile app. Most spaces put their official brand color here.
  • Navigation Color highlights the active section in the navigation sidebar.
  • Background Color applies to all pages in the portal and mobile app. Most spaces pick a grey or lighter tone so text stands out.

Mix and match until the combination fits your brand.

Add a favicon

The favicon is the small icon that appears next to the tab title, so members can spot your portal at a glance. Upload it under Settings > Experience Hub > Branding. Most clients use a .png transparent square version of their logo.

Upload a hero image

The hero image shows before members log in and again at the top of the portal once they’re inside. Upload it under Settings > Experience Hub > Branding. Most spaces use a photo of their building or interior.

Configure your welcome widget

The Welcome widget pairs your hero image with custom text to greet members. Go to Settings > Experience Hub > Member Pages, scroll to the Dashboard section, and click Configure under Welcome Widget. Add a Title and Subtitle that members see when they log in.

Organize your main menu

You have full control over the main menu and the links members see. Turn features on or off with the associated checkboxes.

Go to Settings > Experience Hub > Member Pages and review the pages and functions available to activate or deactivate.

Scroll further to reorder the menu. Use the cogwheel next to each page and click Edit to change its title, icon, and order. Pages with the same number are ordered alphabetically.

Write a welcome post

Greet members in your digital space the way you’d greet someone walking through the door. Write a short welcome post with a photo of your space or team. From the Admin Portal, go to Collaboration / Posts and click Add Post.

Select Pin to top so it’s the first thing members see when they log in. You can add an image here too. Click “Add” when you’re happy, and edit it later whenever you need to.

Connect an X account

You can show your company’s X (formerly Twitter) feed inside the portal. Go to Settings > Experience Hub > Member Pages, scroll to the Dashboard section, and click Configure under Twitter Feed. Add your X handle and set how many posts to display at once.

Brand your meeting rooms

Once your meeting rooms and hourly rates are set up, add photos. In the Admin Portal, go to Space / Meeting Rooms, click the cog wheel next to a room, open the Calendar tab, and upload images. Photos help members recognize the room they’re booking.

Add the amenities of each room too. You can set these when creating the meeting room rates, and they show up on the calendar at booking time.

Customize your how-to guides

Post body:
A virtual coworking office service gives a business a professional address, mail handling, and on-demand access to your space, without the client renting a permanent desk or office. For operators, it’s a way to earn recurring revenue from people who need a business presence but not a full-time seat, and it brings in leads you can later convert to memberships.

In our previous post, we outlined what a virtual office is. Here we cover how to promote and sell the service online: through marketplaces and through your own website.

How do you sell a virtual office on marketplaces?

Online marketplaces connect providers and buyers. You list your offering, and users filter, compare, and choose from a range of options in one place.

For a virtual office, these platforms are one of the most useful lead-generation channels. They pull steady traffic, which gives your service exposure to buyers who are already searching for a business address. The trade-off is that you compete on their terms: their branding, their pricing display, and often a referral fee or reseller split.

Here are some of the most established virtual office marketplaces.

Davinci Virtual

Davinci is one of the better-known marketplaces for virtual offices, on-demand meeting space, and live answering. It runs on a reseller model: coworking spaces that join the network decide which services to offer and set their own price, and Davinci sells them on its platform. The company has operated since 2006 and lists 1,000+ locations worldwide, so a listing puts your space in front of a large existing audience.

Alliance Virtual Offices

Alliance Virtual Offices lists 1,400+ locations. The offer covers a business address, hourly or daily office and meeting room rental, live receptionist services, and a VoIP phone system, all on flexible monthly agreements. Behind each address is a staffed business center with onsite meeting rooms and workspace, which is the credibility signal most virtual office buyers are paying for.

Instant Offices

Instant Offices, part of The Instant Group, is one of the larger office brokers connecting workspace providers and users. It handles more than 5,000 inquiries a month and has market data on flexible office rates across 2,200+ cities, so beyond lead generation you also get benchmarking you can use when pricing your own service.

Same Day Virtual Offices

Same Day Virtual Offices provides mail and answering services aimed mainly at small businesses and individuals. Their packages bundle a virtual office and live answering with a business phone number.

Before you list anywhere, check the fee structure and how much control you keep over pricing and the customer relationship. A marketplace listing wins you reach; your own website wins you the margin and the member data.

How do you promote a virtual office on your own website?

Marketplaces aside, your own marketing brings in leads you fully control. It takes more time and, in some cases, more budget, but the customer and the recurring revenue stay with you. Our post with 20 marketing ideas for coworking spaces goes deeper on tactics.

Paid advertising

Paid ads reach a large audience and bring results fast, but they cost money for every click. They tend to pay off for established spaces with multiple locations and a stable budget. For a single new location, the return often isn’t there yet, so start small and watch your cost per lead before scaling spend.

Content marketing

Content marketing builds brand awareness, search rankings, and leads. It costs less than paid advertising, sometimes nothing but your time, but it’s slow to show results. Done well, it earns long-term relationships with prospects and members. Practical starting points: a page targeting “virtual office [your city],” a clear pricing table, and answers to the questions buyers actually ask (mail handling, business registration, meeting room access).

OfficeRnD Flex

OfficeRnD Flex is coworking and flex space management software that lets you sell memberships and services online, bill automatically, and give members a branded digital experience. For a virtual office, that means you can take the service to market and handle checkout without extra tools.

OfficeRnD Flex lets you build an e-commerce checkout on your marketing website. Create a branded public page, list the services you choose (a virtual office, plus low-commitment options like day passes), and link to that page from your site. Visitors get a fast, self-serve way to buy.

Offer your virtual office to members through the Member Portal:

The OfficeRnD Flex Member Portal makes it easy to upsell existing members with add-on services like a virtual office. There are two ways to do it:

Members see the services you list in the portal, add them to their plan in a couple of clicks, and get them included in their current or next invoice automatically.

You can embed an external page (for example, a virtual office provider’s registration page) in the OfficeRnD Flex member apps and make it look like a native part of the web portal or mobile app. Members register for the service directly if you choose to automate it. For more detail, see our post on virtual offices (scroll to the last section).

Name: What Is Virtual Office And How Coworking Spaces Can Use It
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: A virtual office gives a business a professional address, mail handling, and on-demand access to meeting rooms without renting a desk or signing a lease. For coworking operators, it’s one of the few products you can sell past the physical capacity of your building.
Post body:
A virtual office gives a business a professional address, mail handling, and on-demand access to meeting rooms without renting a desk or signing a lease. For coworking operators, it’s one of the few products you can sell past the physical capacity of your building.

Most operators lean on desks, private offices, and memberships for revenue. Those are capped by square footage. A virtual office isn’t, which is why it keeps showing up in conversations about how flex spaces grow margin. Virtual offices, mail handling, and business address services have become among the most scalable revenue streams in coworking, and in some portfolios they generate revenue comparable to that of a smaller physical location while using almost no space.

The market backs that up. Independent estimates put the global virtual office market in the range of 25 to 40 billion USD, with forecasts of double-digit annual growth through the early 2030s driven by remote and hybrid work. So the question for operators is simple: how do you provide value and generate revenue from members and prospects who rarely, or never, set foot in your space?

The answer is a service that’s been in the executive-office playbook for decades: the virtual office. More companies want a business address without paying for a desk, and it can bring in steady, growing recurring revenue for your space.

What is a virtual office?

A virtual office is part of the flexible workspace industry that provides businesses with any combination of services, space, and technology, without those businesses bearing the capital expenses of owning, leasing, or licensing an actual office.

The typical virtual office product bundles three core services:

  • Business mailbox and address
  • Mail management
  • Meeting room time

Adding a virtual office to your business model helps in three areas:

  1. Offering a monetizable service to existing members
  2. Generating leads that may upgrade to full-time office space later
  3. Driving more business for your meeting rooms

Here’s the scenario in practice. A professional or company uses your address as their business address without physically using your space. Some use it only as a vanity address because they need to claim a location as their own. Others use it to receive mail. When mail or packages arrive, you sort them, hold them, and forward, scan, shred, or release them for pickup depending on the plan they signed up for.

Why would someone need a virtual office?

The service has been around for decades, and people still ask why anyone needs it. Here’s who benefits, split between the members you already have and the customers you don’t yet.

Existing members

Members who work from home most of the week still receive mail and packages at their business address, which is your space. They can’t always come in to collect it. You can manage that for them.

You can offer mail management for free as added value, betting it strengthens the relationship and pays off later. Or you can charge for it depending on how you price your plans.

For example, you might process a set number of mail parcels free of charge, then charge for volume above that, or sell weekly, bi-weekly, or monthly forwarding plans at fixed rates. With a lot of members and a high volume of mail, software to run the process is worth it. More on that below.

Potential customers

Plenty of people don’t need or can’t afford a physical office but still want a professional business address. Three reasons come up most:

  1. Credibility
  2. Privacy
  3. Full-time availability

A company’s business address shapes its reputation. Placing your office in a well-known building can help win customers, build credibility, or just make a good first impression.

Privacy is the second reason. A virtual office keeps a founder’s home address off public records and directories when they work from home.

And if a person or their team isn’t available to receive mail at home or their current office, a virtual office hands that responsibility to your front desk.

Registration adds a fourth reason. Founders setting up an LLC often need a physical address in the state where they incorporate. A virtual office supplies that address without them relocating or leasing space, which is common for businesses registering in one state while operating from another.

How do you make money from a virtual office?

Virtual office pricing usually runs from about 40 to 200 USD per month for core services, with add-ons stacked on top. Because you’re not giving up a desk, most of that is margin.

A virtual office also expands your target market beyond the area around your building. Many companies want to claim an address in a different city, state, or country from where they actually operate.

You monetize it two ways: sell it as an add-on to current customers, and use it to bring in new ones.

How you price it is up to you. In most cases there’s a base price for the business address, and every extra service builds on top: mail forwarding, mail scanning, shredding, phone answering, and so on. Charging separately for mail volume, additional business entities, and phone answering is where a lot of operators find room, and discounted pricing for multiple entities captures revenue from serial entrepreneurs without pushing them away.

A virtual office can also help you reopen old leads. Prospects who looked at a full membership but couldn’t justify the cost are worth a follow-up: offer them a virtual office as a starting point, then convert them to physical space later.

How can you set up a virtual office with OfficeRnD?

OfficeRnD Flex is the coworking and flex space platform operators use to automate billing, memberships, bookings, and member services in one place. To run virtual offices inside it, OfficeRnD Flex integrates with PilotoMail, a mail management platform built for coworking operators and mailroom teams.

The integration gives you self-serve virtual mailboxes and streamlined billing. Your client’s mailbox actions sync into their monthly OfficeRnD Flex invoice, so mail requests and forwarding are billed automatically instead of tracked by hand. Members get to view and manage their mail and packages from anywhere.

You can find setup details on the integration page.

Virtual office vs coworking space: what’s the difference?

They get compared because they overlap, but they solve different problems. A coworking membership gives someone a place to work most days plus a business address. A virtual office gives the address, mail handling, and meeting room access without requiring anyone to show up.

The two aren’t mutually exclusive. A common setup: a member uses a virtual office as their business foundation and buys coworking day access for the days they want to be on-site. For operators, that’s the upsell path, virtual customers who later convert into desk or office members.

Name: 4 Coworking Apps to Sell Your Meeting Rooms Online
Author: asen-stoyanchev
Short cards description: Coworking marketplaces and apps put your meeting rooms in front of people who are already searching for a room to book. That’s traffic you don’t have to generate yourself. Post body:
Coworking marketplaces and apps put your meeting rooms in front of people who are already searching for a room to book. That’s traffic you don’t have to generate yourself. Alongside your own marketing (content, SEO, lead generation and paid ads), listing on the right platforms is one of the fastest ways to fill idle rooms and pull in new members.

A coworking app is a booking platform that lets professionals discover, reserve, and pay for shared workspace and meeting rooms across many independent operators, usually by the hour or day. For an operator, a listing means your rooms show up where demand already exists.

Two rules apply everywhere. Use good photos. Write clear, specific descriptions. Listings with weak images and thin copy get skipped, no matter how good the room is.

Here are four platforms worth listing on, plus how to sell rooms straight from your own website.

LiquidSpace

LiquidSpace is one of the largest real-time networks for renting flexible office space and meeting rooms. It connects your space with individuals, teams, start-ups, and large corporate clients, and lists your rooms where they can be found and booked instantly.

Creating a profile is free. You list desks, offices, and meeting rooms by the hour, day, month, or longer, and you set your own terms and pricing. Set up your spaces once, sync them to your internal calendar to display real-time availability, and receive instant bookings. LiquidSpace charges a tiered host fee per booking rather than a flat listing cost, so check the current host terms before you publish.

Coworker

Coworker is a global marketplace for discovering and booking coworking desks, private offices, and meeting rooms. Website visitors can browse, compare amenities, request a booking, schedule a tour, or reserve directly where you’ve enabled it.

The reach is the draw. Coworker’s network holds more than 25,000 spaces, with over 300 new spaces joining each month. You can claim your space for free to get verified, respond to reviews, and update your details, and paid listing options add more visibility on top of that.

Croissant

Croissant is an app that promotes your shared workspace to small teams, entrepreneurs, freelancers, and digital workers. Members check in through the app and drop into partner spaces on demand.

Listing is free with no setup fees or monthly charges. You keep full control through the partner dashboard: set available seats per day, block dates, and adjust availability in real time. Croissant pays you for each member who checks in, with monthly payouts and a statement showing every visit. If you have conference rooms, you can list those too.

If you run OfficeRnD Flex, this one connects directly. Croissant’s OfficeRnD integration syncs conference room availability in real time between the two systems, so bookings stay accurate on both sides without manual updates.

OfficeRnD Flex

OfficeRnD Flex is a management platform for coworking and flex spaces that helps operators run day-to-day operations and grow revenue. Its Public Calendar and Public Sign-up features make your meeting rooms bookable directly from your own website.

The public booking calendar exposes your rooms’ live availability so non-members can book a room on their own. Every booking syncs in real time with the availability of your resources, and you can charge and invoice each purchase directly. You set the permissions: who can book, when, at what rate, and under which cancellation policy.

Selling rooms from your own site is useful when a prospect is in a hurry and needs a room right now. No back-and-forth, no waiting on a reply. They book, they pay, they’re in.

Which coworking app should you use to sell meeting rooms?

Use more than one. Marketplaces like LiquidSpace and Coworker bring you demand you can’t reach alone, and Croissant fills seats and rooms through on-demand check-ins. Your own public booking calendar in OfficeRnD Flex captures the people who already found you and just want to book. The listings feed each other: the more places your rooms appear, the more bookings you close.

Post body:
A coworking app is any software that automates a specific part of running a flex space, from front-desk check-in and door access to payments, member perks, and printing. Running a coworking space means juggling billing, meeting room bookings, facility management, and member well-being all at once. You can’t drop those tasks, but you can automate most of them with the right apps.

Doing so adds value for your members, lifts satisfaction, and keeps you competitive. Here are 5 of the best coworking apps for 2026, plus one bonus that ties them together.

1. The Receptionist for iPad

How you welcome and check in members and visitors shapes the impression you make as a brand. The smoother that process, the better.

The Receptionist is a visitor management app that lets you customize and automate the daily check-in processes in your coworking space. It signs in members and visitors at the front desk and directs them to where they need to go.

Visitor management software gives you a clear record of who’s in your space and when. It also removes the need for someone to staff the front desk at all times.

2. SALTO KS

Access control is another piece every successful coworking business needs to get right.

SALTO KS is a cloud-based access control system for flexible workspaces. It lets you define who goes where and when across a building.

You can grant designated access to members, staff, or delivery and cleaning services whenever it’s appropriate for them to enter. The mobile app means members open doors with a digital key on their phone, and you can adjust access from anywhere.

By integrating SALTO KS with a coworking management platform you can modify access by contract, company, or any other criteria you choose, and members get access automatically the moment they join.

3. Stripe

Collecting payments is the core of your business. Automating it takes a large chunk of admin off your plate.

Stripe is one of the leading payment gateways for accepting payments and managing your business online. You can collect payments for offices and desks, bookings, and any additional services you offer.

That saves time and removes friction from getting paid.

4. Included.co

With Included.co you can offer product and service discounts to your members under your own brand. For your community it’s a worthwhile perk, and for you it builds your brand and adds value to your membership.

You can share or embed member benefits in your newsletter, onboarding, member portal, or website. In late 2024, Included.co partnered with Builtfirst to launch a coworking perks marketplace, giving spaces a white-labeled, embeddable catalog of SaaS and service discounts.

5. ezeep

Printing matters more in coworking than people expect, and it gets complicated fast. For your members’ sanity and your own, simplify it as much as you can.

ezeep is cloud-based printing software that lets members print from any device, in any location, to any printer. It moves the whole workflow to the cloud, so nobody worries about drivers or operating systems. Members print from a browser or the app, and every page is tracked and billed to the right account automatically.

Extra tip: Check out the 5 rules for finding the right printer for your coworking space.

Bonus app: Bring it together with OfficeRnD Flex

The five apps above each solve one problem well. A coworking management platform connects them and gives you a single view of how your space is used and where your revenue comes from.

OfficeRnD Flex is a management platform for coworking and flex spaces that automates billing, meeting room management, reporting, and more. It comes as a web platform plus a suite of member-facing mobile apps, and it connects members, operators, and owners across 2,500-plus locations worldwide.

It integrates with the tools on this list, including Stripe, SALTO KS, and ezeep, so members get access, printing, and payments set up automatically when they join. That means fewer manual tasks, a clearer picture of your business metrics, and a better digital experience for members.

There are plenty of platforms on the market, so pick the one that fits your business model and objectives. 

Where does AI fit into your coworking app stack?

Most coworking spaces don’t have a lead quality problem. They have a lead timing problem: an inquiry lands at 9 PM and your team picks it up the next morning, by which point the prospect has toured somewhere else.

That’s the gap AI Hub addresses. It’s an AI automation layer built into OfficeRnD Flex, and its first agent, the AI Sales Agent, connects to your website contact forms and shared inbox, responds within seconds, qualifies the lead, and books a tour, using your real availability and product catalog. If you run multiple locations or handle high inbound volume, that’s the kind of repetitive, time-sensitive work worth automating first.

Post body:
We’re thrilled to announce that we raised $3 million to speed up our growth and take the OfficeRnD product and services to a whole new level. The new venture round is led by Flashpoint Venture Capital and LAUNCHub Ventures.

We’ve been growing exponentially over the last years, constantly improving our product and significantly expanding our team and customer base worldwide. As for today, we’re happy and proud of having 50+ teammates and more than 500 customers operating 1000+ locations that service more than 100 000 members.

We put an enormous effort into building the most robust and reliable flexible workspace management platform. And we want to continue delivering the best.

Here’s what to expect:

User experience, product functionality, and service excellence

The new funding will go straight into developing our product even better and faster. 

We’ll take the user experience, the functionality depth of our products and the services we provide to a new level and achieve our long-term vision – to make flexible working the way of working.

Because we believe that by completely transforming the concept of how we lease, rent, and use office space, the flexible workspace model is a movement that’s reshaping the future of work.

For us, the office should be more than physical space. Instead, it should be a space for innovation, collaboration, and enhanced productivity. Not only serving our immediate needs by accommodating essential amenities but adding value on top—by adopting hospitality as a core element of the workspace business, and by providing access to a strong community of like-minded professionals.

It’s what we call Space as a Service – The Workspace Evolution. An evolution that’s already happening.

Coworking and flexible workspaces have been growing rapidly over the last several years. As technological advances make remote work easier, it is expected to boom in the following years, disrupting the multi-billion dollar office space rental market. More and more Commercial Real Estate owners create flexible offices as this allows increased yields as well as makes their offer more attractive to tenants. Small and large businesses have the option to rent on more flexible terms than the typical multi-year lease. 

But setting up and operating a flexible workspace involves servicing hundreds of people and making sure they are billed correctly, can reserve shared resources and have access to the right places. The community element and making sure that members get along nicely with each other is also a significant challenge.

To solve these challenges, we’ve built a software platform that automates all key business processes and integrates other workspace technologies such as access control, wi-fi, printing and more. To provide an end-to-end solution, we also offer a suite of white-label apps that help the members of flexible workspaces engage with their office and the workspace community.

Having all this, we dare to say that our products play a key role in shaping the future of flexible working. With the new funding, we’ll build on top of this not only in terms of product but in terms of services and global presence too!

Thank you!

OfficeRnD customers, you are appreciated. Through our imperfections, you’ve kept the faith, and you’ve made us what we are today. We are wholly committed to giving you what you want and need, and making you more successful. We have more passion, energy, and resources than we’ve ever had, and can’t wait to get all these new things into your hands.

Don’t take it from us! See what our investors think:

“We believe that the way we work is currently changing in a significant way. As technology enables us to work remotely, workers are less keen to sit in cubicles and companies are exploring alternatives like coworking spaces and flexible offices to differentiate themselves. In order to serve these clients well, Commercial Real Estate owners need a technology enabler that allows them to manage operations efficiently. We looked into the market and were very impressed with Miro and the OfficeRnD team, which managed to build a market leader in the US and UK markets, incubating their R&D team in Bulgaria. With our investment they will be able to scale their R&D and Sales team further to be able to service even more happy customers.

—Alex Konoplyasty, Managing Partner of Flashpoint Venture Capital

We are among the first investors in OfficeRnD and we made a bet in this company when the term future of work was not even a buzzword. Miroslav has proven to be an amazing founder, who managed to build a strong team and the best product in the space, loved by their clients. The transformation in this industry is happening now and we are happy to continue being part of OfficeRnD’s journey.

—Todor Breshkov, Partner at LAUNCHub Ventures
